articleTitle: Design and evaluation of a WR-15 (50 to 75 GHz) microcalorimeter
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: The design and correction factor evaluation of a WR-15 (50 to 75 GHz) rectangular waveguide microcalorimeter is presented. This new microcalorimeter will be the US national standard for power from 50 to 75 GHz. It can measure the effective efficiency of a wider variety of transfer standards than can the previous microcalorimeter. It has also been designed so that its correction factor can be experimentally evaluated by multiple techniques.

articleTitle: Extending ac-dc current transfer measurement to 100 A, 100 kHz
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: This paper describes the design and verification of current shunts for AC-DC transfer measurements in the range 20 A to 100 A. The measured AC-DC current transfer difference of the 100 A shunt is -36 muA/A at 100 kHz with an uncertainty of 200 muA/A.

articleTitle: Subpicoampere current source based on a digital-to-analog converter
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A current source based on a voltage ramp generated by a 16-bit digital-to-analog converter and a differentiating capacitor has been developed in MIKES. The system is suitable for generating currents from 1 fA to 100 pA. Standard deviation of average dU/dt:s of 70 ramps during an overnight measurement is as low as 1 ppm.

articleTitle: Precision differential sampling measurements of low frequency voltages synthesized with an AC Programmable Josephson Voltage Standard
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Sampling is a promising technique for comparing the stepwise-approximated sine waves synthesized by an AC Programmable Josephson Voltage Standard to the sinusoidal voltages of a secondary source at low frequencies (a few hundred hertz or less). This paper describes a differential method that uses an integrating sampling voltmeter to precisely determine the amplitude and phase of high purity sine wave voltages by comparing them to quantum-accurate waveforms.

articleTitle: Remote power management and meter-reading system based on ARM microprocessor
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A power load management system based on ARM-7 microcontroller and GPRS is presented in this paper. The proposed system consists of electronic KWH meter, intelligent management terminal (IMT) and management centre. The intelligent terminal is sued to acquire information from KWH meter, control the energy-consuming device and communicate with management centre via GPRS network. How to implement the IMT by using ARM-7 microcontroller and GPRS telecommunication module is discussed in detail. Also the software design of the terminal with high performance embedded real-time operating system muC/OS-II is presented in this paper.

articleTitle: AC-DC current transfer difference in CMI
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: This paper describes AC-DC current transfer difference measurement system in CMI which is able to measure AC-DC current differences from 3 mA up to 10 A in the frequency range 10 Hz — 10 kHz.

articleTitle: Influence of busbar geometry on AC current measurement using Rogowski coil
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Readout of a Rogowski coil is affected by external magnetic fields e.g. from the energizing transformer and the return current conductor. The influence of these external magnetic fields on the reading of a high precision Rogowski coil was measured. The results are used to estimate the achievable uncertainty in calibration of current transformers up to 10 kA.

articleTitle: Development of a low-frequency quantum-based AC Power Standard at NRC Canada
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A development of a new low-frequency quantum- based AC Power Standard at the National Research Council of Canada (NRC) is described in the paper. It uses programmable Josephson voltage standard (PJVS) for providing AC voltage with quantum accuracy, highly stable magnetic devices such as voltage and current transformers for scaling output signals to low levels, and digital sampling for comparison of low-level output signal replicas with the PJVS output.

articleTitle: A synchronous sampling system for high precision AC measurements
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: This paper describes a synchronous sampling system which is based on commercial high accuracy I/O devices. The advantage of such devices is their native synchronization capabilities which greatly simplify the timing of the measurements. The type A uncertainty of the system is around 0.3-10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-6</sup> in a 2 minutes measurement time, showing that this system is suitable for a large variety of precision impedance measurements.

articleTitle: Automation of 1 tΩ to 100 tΩ ultra-high resistance measurements at NIST
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: The automation of ultra-high resistance measurements at the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) in the range 1 TOmega to 100 TOmega has been completed with the use of a programmable XY positioning system to facilitate the guarded connection of multiple standard resistors to an automated dual-source bridge. Automated guarded switching that is immune to leakages to ground is critical to the characterization of standard resistors and transfer standards in this range.

articleTitle: Noise-parameter measurement with automated variable terminations
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: NIST has upgraded its measurement capability of noise parameters on low-noise amplifiers with a variable termination unit in the 1 to 12.4 GHz range. Such a unit allows improved time efficiency in the noise-temperature measurements used to de-embed noise parameters of amplifiers. We present measured results for noise parameters of a low noise amplifier in the frequency range of 8 to 12 GHz.

articleTitle: Towards direct closure of the quantum metrological triangle
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: In this paper, plans and progress of a Finnish collaboration towards direct closure of the quantum metrological triangle are presented. The experimental concept and the present status of the main components, including two possibilities of the single charge transport device, Bloch oscillating transistor (BOT) based null detector, and a thin-film cryoresistor, are described.

articleTitle: A capacitance sensor suite evaluation
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: An experiment was set up to evaluate a sensor suite containing an affordable commercially available capacitance to digital converter and a simple custom-built capacitance sensor. A set of surface mount capacitors was thoughtfully assembled for evaluation purposes. The results show good short-term stability, allowing the effective use of the sensor suite in an object classification application.

articleTitle: Calibrating a sampling voltmeter using a binary Josephson system
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A binary Josephson system was used to characterize an 81/2-digit sampling voltmeter. This voltmeter is the heart of the primary standard for power at 50 Hz or 60 Hz at several National Metrology Institutes (NMIs). In this paper, we present first results on the calibration of the voltmeter under conditions that mimic its use in the power standard set-up. Furthermore, the dependence of the root-mean-square (rms) voltage FRMS on the aperture time is presented.

articleTitle: A simplified method for the measurement of magnetic loop antenna factor
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: This paper describes a simplified method of measuring magnetic loop antenna factor over the frequency range from 9 kHz to 30 MHz by using a 3-port Impedance/Gain-Phase Analyzer at NMIA.

articleTitle: Antenna test range imaging using spherical near-field scanning
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Although the theory is straightforward, practical implementation of spherical near-field scanning for evaluating test chambers presents some significant challenges. Among these are the selection of an appropriate probe and the difficulty in minimizing support-structure blockage. We report on recent NIST efforts to address these difficulties and present our most recent results.

articleTitle: Development of quantum hall array resistance standards at NMIJ
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: An experimental device of quantum Hall array resistance standards with a nominal value close to 10 kΩ on the i = 2 plateau and a parallel array of two Hall bars have been developed. The latter array clearly shows quantized Hall resistance of a quarter value of the von Klitzing constant, R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">K</inf> on the i = 2 plateau.

articleTitle: Development of an automated AC-DC transfer measurement system for voltage and current at low frequencies
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: National Physical Laboratory India (NPLI) is the premier research & development center and the National Metrology Institute, which provides traceability in measurements by calibration throughout the country. Low Frequency voltage and current are very important quantities in electrical metrology. The standards for LF voltage and current are established by assigning AC-DC transfer difference to Thermal Converters (TCs) worldwide. The range of frequencies of these standards is from 10 Hz to 1 MHz for the voltage level of 1 V to 1000 V. This paper presents the automation of method of assigning AC-DC transfer difference to thermal converter (from 10 Hz to 1 MHz) makes measurements faster and more accurate through IEEE-488 interface card and cables. The software for this process has been developed using the VEE Pro application, which is a graphical programming environment optimized for use with the electronic instruments. It also minimizes the human involvement and therefore reduces the chances of errors. Using this software, the measurements have been carried on the 6 V TC with respect to 4 V TC at 4 V level in the frequency range from 10 Hz to 1 MHz. The result shows that the automation has been done successfully.

articleTitle: Complete waveform characterization at NIST
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: We present a method for calibrating the voltage that a pulse generator produces at a load at every point in the measured waveform epoch. The calibration includes an equivalent circuit model of the generator so that the user can calculate how the generator will behave when it is connected to different instruments. The calibration also includes a covariance-based uncertainty analysis that provides the uncertainty of each sample and the correlations between the uncertainties at the different time points. Given the calibrated waveform and its covariance matrix, various pulse parameters and their uncertainties can also be calculated.

articleTitle: Progress toward a 1 V pulse-driven ac Josephson voltage standard
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: We present a new record output voltage of 275 mV rms, which is a 25 % improvement over the maximum achieved with previous ac Josephson voltage standard circuits. We demonstrate operating margins for these circuits and use them to measure the harmonic distortion of a commercial digitizer. Having exceeded the threshold of 125 mV rms for a single array of Josephson junctions, we propose an eight-array circuit capable of achieving 1 V rms.

articleTitle: On the use of windows for measurements of R.M.S., active power and harmonic parameters.
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Weighing windows have been suggested so as to cut the error that non-coherent sampling induce in the measurement of r.m.s., power and harmonic parameters. The link between the weighing and the Swerelein algorithms is shown. The paper also presents an algorithm for finding the amplitude and phase of harmonics based on the frequency characteristic of the used window. The suggested windows allow the reduction of the error due to non-coherent sampling to 0.1..0.3ldr10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-6</sup> with the measurement time of 2.5 to 3.5 periods of fundamental harmonic.

articleTitle: A high audio-frequency inductive voltage divider standard up to 100 kHz
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A high audio-frequency inductive voltage divider (IVD) and its calibration system at the frequencies from 10 kHz to 100 kHz have been developed in order to establish the high audio-frequency ac metrology. Design of the constructed IVD and its calibration circuit are described.

articleTitle: A new synchronous method for attenuation measurement system
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Audio frequency substitution with inductive voltage divider (IVD) as reference standard is the most important attenuator calibration system in which a lock-in amplifier is widely used as phase sensitive detector. In order to obtain synchronous signal for lock-in amplifier, a new simple system structures with good stability was developed in NIM (China). Its principle and experiment data are discussed in the paper.

articleTitle: Rabi frequency measurement for microwave power standard using double resonance spectrum
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: In this paper we describe a basic experiment with the aim of developing a new type of microwave power standard that utilizes atomic resonances. The microwave field strength is determined from the oscillation of the population of atomic quantum states caused by the interaction between a microwave and Cs atoms (Rabi oscillation). A rectangular Cs glass cell was developed for this experiment and inserted in a WR90 waveguide. The observed frequencies of the Rabi oscillation were proportional to the microwave field strength, which demonstrated the feasibility of the new microwave power standard.

articleTitle: Uncertainty analysis for noise-parameter measurements
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A brief summary is presented for the uncertainty analysis for measurements of noise parameters of amplifiers and transistors, in both connectorized (coaxial) and on-wafer environments. We treat both the X-parameters, which are based on the wave representation of the noise correlation matrix, and the traditional IEEE noise parameters.

articleTitle: RF power measurement calculable primary standard
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A calculable RF power standard has been studied in order to evaluate its efficiency eta. A time-domain simulator has been optimized together with an analytical approach to model the RF detector. A coplanar thermistor mount prototype has been realized and the results are presented.

articleTitle: AC magnetic flux density standards in the low frequency range
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: An AC magnetic flux density standard system was constructed for calibration in KRISS magnetometers and for the testing of the magnetic field characteristics of sensors and materials in the frequency range below 20 kHz. This system consists of an AC magnetic field converter, a Helmholtz coil, a voltage comparator, a voltmeter, a standard resistor, and a computer with a program for automatic measurement. The expanded uncertainty (k=2) is 0.2% in the range of 1 Hz to 20 kHz.

articleTitle: A setup for AC voltage synthesis using a SINIS Josephson array
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A setup for low frequency ac voltage synthesis using a SINIS Josephson array has been realized. Transients in the synthesis have been measured and dc measurement tests have been performed.

articleTitle: Design of a turn-key 10 V Programmable Josephson Voltage Standard system
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: NIST is designing a 10 V Programmable Josephson Voltage Standard (PJVS) system with an improved microwave design and arrays of stacked Nb<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub>Si<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-x</sub>-barrier Josephson junctions. For this new design a "ground-up" approach was used that takes into account all system issues in order to produce a robust 10 V system. By improving the uniformity of the microwave drive along the length of each array, constant-voltage steps with a larger current range are generated allowing the use of smaller critical current junctions. Smaller critical currents are important for lowering the total overall power dissipated on chip. Reducing power dissipation also increases the operating margins. Thus, all aspects of the design are interrelated and important for an optimized system.

articleTitle: The serial and parallel self-calibration of DC comparator up to 5kA
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: The deviation of serial and parallel ratios of direct current (DCC) comparator is investigated. By matching the currents passing the paralleled windings with the same nominal value, the deviation of the ratio of a group paralleled windings to the same group serial windings could be reduced to a negligible level. A suit of DCC with serial and parallel structure was developed to build the traceability of DC current up to 5 kA with uncertainties better than 1 times 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-6</sup>.

articleTitle: Ac-dc current transfer difference at BEV
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: This paper describes the method used at BEV to determine the frequency dependence of thermal current converters at 10 mA in the frequency range 10 Hz to 1 MHz.

articleTitle: DC and low frequency humidity dependence of an air-gap capacitor
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: We have measured both the 0.01 Hz (quasi-DC) and 1.0 kHz value of a room temperature air-gap capacitor as a function of environment (pressure, temperature, humidity). A huge difference in the humidity dependence was discovered in both measurements. This proves that surface layers containing adsorbed water have a significant effect on the frequency dependence of the capacitance value of air-gap capacitors.

articleTitle: High resistance scaling from 10 kΩ and QHR standards using a cryogenic current comparator
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: We describe a cryogenic current comparator (CCC) bridge for resistance scaling that provides improved measurement uncertainty over a range of resistance values from 100 kOmega to 1 GOmega. This CCC is designed for high resistance scaling based directly on a quantized Hall resistance (QHR) standard as well as comparisons of resistance ratios of 1, 10 and 100. The QHR-to-decade-value winding ratio offset is chosen so as to approximately cancel the offset produced by resistive decade windings.

articleTitle: A self-calibrating high-precision current transformer
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A self-calibrating current transformer with nominal ratio 10 A to 100 mA, intended for low frequencies applications, was developed. It has 100 independent primary windings to be connected in series or parallel, so that it can be configured as 100:1 or 1:1 transformer (all windings in series). This last ratio permits autocalibration. Error sources are analyzed, and it is shown that differences between parallel and series configurations have uncertainties lower than 1 part in 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sup>.

articleTitle: Uncertainties of VNA S-parameter measurements applying the Short-Open-Load-reciprocal (SOLR) calibration method
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: For the 7-term SOLR calibration method to calibrate a four-sampler vector network analyser (VNA), the deviations of the seven error terms, as well as of the the measured S-parameters are determined due to the deviations of the reflections of the calibration elements (Short, Open and Load) from their true values. For the SOLR calibration, a reciprocal unknown network is used instead of a known Through. The influence of a slightly non-reciprocal network on error term and S-parameter deviations is also considered.

articleTitle: Direct comparison transfer microwave power sensor calibration system
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: This paper describes the development of a microwave power sensor calibration system using the direct comparison transfer method with a resistive power splitter. The system setup, its uncertainty analysis and measurement results are discussed.

articleTitle: Asymmetric double 2DEGs As a basis of quantum hall resistance standards
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: We study growth and magnetotransport properties of Ga(Al)As based asymmetric double two-dimensional electron gases (2DEG) consisting of a quantum well stacked on top of a heterojunction. We show that the electron densities of the two parallel 2DEG channels can be reliably matched by variation of a single growth parameter. Metrological quality of the resistance quantization of the two parallel quantum Hall channels at filling factor 2 is demonstrated.

articleTitle: Practical scanner for voltage metrology
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A switching device with low thermal electromotive forces is a core apparatus in all voltage standard laboratories where the unit must be maintained with high accuracy. Switching is essential in the pair intercomparison measurements required to maintain a voltage standard with multiple references and for the dissemination of the unit. Although various low- thermal switching equipment are available commercially, most of them are not suited for voltage metrology, making it difficult to find an acceptable tradeoff between, accuracy, cost, reliability and ease of use. In the following a prototype of a practical USB-controlled device for low thermal interconnection and polarity reversal of reference standards is described.

articleTitle: Measurement of AC current with coaxial current shunts
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: New coaxial current shunts that cover AC current range from 10 mA to 20 A have been developed. The advantage of new current shunts is a very low frequency dependence up to 30 kHz and very stable DC resistance which makes it possible to use current shunts for very accurate direct measurement of the AC current over the AC voltage drop on the known resistance.

articleTitle: Thermal-noise-limited optical cavity
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A pair of optical cavities are designed to be insensitive to both temperature fluctuations and mechanical vibrations. The fractional frequency stability of a laser locked to one of these cavities reaches a floor of 2 times 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-15</sup> for averaging times in the is attributed to range 0.5 s - 100 s. This limit Brownian motion of the mirrors.

articleTitle: Precision measurement of harmonic current and power at industrial frequency
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: The precision measurement for harmonic current and power up to 60<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> order and some validating experiments is reported. The uncertainty of harmonics current reference to fundamental is less than 36 μA/A (k=2) for range up to 50 A. The uncertainty of harmonic power reference to the fundamental apparent power is less than 42 μW/VA (k=2) for voltage and current range up to 500 V and 50 A.

articleTitle: Testing calculable resistors of quadrifilar design
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Quadrifilar resistors with nominal values of 100 Omega, 1000 Omega and 10000 Omega, as well as a 100 Omega coaxial resistor, have been realized and their frequency dependences have been calculated from their constructional parameters. With the aim of experimentally verifying correctness of mathematical models used in these calculations, frequency dependences of ratios of parallel equivalent resistances of the realized resistors have been measured by means of a four terminal-pair transformer bridge.

articleTitle: A current-comparator-based high-voltage inductance bridge
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: An overview of the development of a current-comparator-based high-voltage inductance bridge at the National Research Council of Canada (NRC) for the accurate measurements of load losses of large high voltage inductive loads at low power factor operating conditions, such as, large high voltage power transformers and shunt reactors, will be presented. The bridge has ratio uncertainties of less than 10times10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-6</sup> in both magnitude and phase.

articleTitle: RF measurements of nanoscale devices: Challenges and opportunities
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: This invited talk will describe some of the opportunities and challenges associated with RF measurements of nanoelectronic devices.

articleTitle: Harmonic power standard at NIM and its compensation algorithm
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: For calibration of analyzer of harmonic voltage, current and power under non-sinusoidal condition at fundamental in industrial frequency, a harmonic power standard has been built at NIM, in which Non-Integer-Period sampling is applied. Its setup, algorithm, and whole uncertainty are reported.

articleTitle: A PC based setup to determine temperature coefficient of standard inductors using difference voltage measurement technique
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: This paper describes a setup to determine the temperature coefficient of standards inductors. Proposed method is based on Transformer Ratio Bridge and difference voltage measurement technique. The temperature coefficient of three inductors of value 1 mH (GR 1482) was measured by this method in the temperature range of 22degC to 27degC, which lies between 42 to 47 ppm/ degC with deviation of plusmn 5 ppm. This method also gives the time taken by inductors to get stabilized against change in temperature.

articleTitle: APMP key comparison of Ka-band antenna gain (APMP.EM.RF-K3.F)
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: An APMP key comparison of power gain for Ka-band (26.5 GHz - 40 GHz) horn antennas has been being carried out between KRISS and NMIJ. This paper describes the comparison and its progress so far. Measurement results will be presented at the conference.

articleTitle: Research on simulation impedance
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: The impedance characteristics of resistance, capacitance and inductance can be simulated to calibrate Impedance Bridge by means of setting the amplitude ratio of voltage to current. In this paper we analyze the principles of voltage controlled and current controlled simulation impedance. The experiment and data are given. We propose the new concept of Digital Simulation Impedance (DSI) which is simulated by a digital waveform generator to acquire the waveforms of impedance voltage and current whose amplitude ratio and phase difference can be reproduced and saved in digital values. The advantages are wide range and frequency, program-controlling and digital correction.

articleTitle: Direct 10 V Josephson Voltage Standard comparison between a programmable sinis array and a conventional sis array
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: In December 2007, a comparison of the 10 V Josephson Array Voltage Standard (JAVS) of the LNE was performed with that of the BIPM in the framework of BIPM.EM-KlO.b comparison. During the week allotted to the exercise, the measurement setup was optimized to achieve a relative voltage difference of 7times10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-12</sup> within a relative Type A uncertainty of 8times10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-12</sup>. We then took the opportunity to carry out a direct comparison of a 10 V PTB programmable array against the LNE JAVS. We report on the experiments performed to establish the uncertainty budget. We present the characterization of a 10 V SINIS array. We conclude with the results of a direct comparison against the LNE JAVS.

articleTitle: Single-junction thermal voltage converters with reduced uncertainties at frequencies up to 1 MHz
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: The paper presents a new realisation of standards for AC-DC difference at voltages from 1 V to 4 V and frequencies up to 1 MHz with standard uncertainties less than 5 muV/V at 1 MHz.

articleTitle: Uncertainty estimation of phase shift of voltage dividers and shunts measured by sampling approach
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: The uncertainty of phase shift determined through DFT of sampling data for the voltage dividers and shunts in the harmonic power standard at NIM [1] is reported.

articleTitle: Proposal of a new method of measurement of the quantized hall resistance with a Binary Josephson array in a bridge configuration
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A new method to compare the Quantized Hall Resistance (QHR) with a conventional resistance standard is proposed. This new method uses a Binary junction programmable Josephson array specifically designed to have a center tap to simultaneously measure the voltage of the QHR and the test resistance. This new method is expected to compete in uncertainty with the Cryogenic Current Comparator at lower cost.

articleTitle: Calibration of high voltage resistor dividers
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: This paper describes the calibration of a high voltage resistor divider, using a comparison method. A capacitive and electronic divider or a standard instrument voltage transformer serves as a standard. The difference is evaluated either by means of a special system or by means of a lock-in amplifier.

articleTitle: Improvements in the NIST Johnson noise thermometry system
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: We have developed a Johnson noise thermometry system that is calibrated by precision waveforms synthesized with a quantized voltage noise source (QVNS). Significant improvements to the QVNS and the cross-correlation measurement electronics have dramatically reduced systematic errors and measurement uncertainty. We describe some of these improvements and discuss the potential for this system to contribute to the redefinition of the Boltzmann constant.

articleTitle: Calibrated broadband electrical characterization of nanowires
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: We present a technique for broadband electrical characterization of nanowires up to 40 GHz. The technique relies on established on-wafer, microwave calibration methods as well as direct measurement of the capacitive coupling that is in parallel with the nano-wire admittance. GaN nanowire devices are used to demonstrate the measurement technique and their response is found to depend strongly on the quality of electrical contacts and the geometry of the nanowire network.

articleTitle: Improvements of the AC quantum voltmeter
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: The AC quantum voltmeter, an instrument for measuring AC waveforms by comparing them to a Josephson waveform, has been enhanced. Two different improvements to the signal-to-noise ratio are presented. The signal amplitude has been significantly increased by using 10-V Josephson arrays. The noise contribution has been reduced by adding a preamplifier at the input of the sampling null detector.

articleTitle: AC power standard using a programmable Josephson voltage standard
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: This paper describes the implementation of a new quantum-based system for the generation of 120 V, 5 A, sinusoidal active and reactive power over the 50 Hz to 400 Hz frequency range. The system accurately relates the spectral amplitudes and phases of the voltage and current waveforms of the generated power to a programmable Josephson voltage standard (PJVS) using a novel differential sampling technique. The system also employs a new voltage amplifier that performs self-calibration and correction of gain and phase errors. Details of the system design, measurement techniques, and significant sources of error are presented.

articleTitle: Realization of ac-dc current transfer difference to 1 MHz at SP
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: This paper describes the realization of AC-DC current transfer difference at SP with emphasis on the realization at high frequencies, which is based on modeling of single junction thermal converters by their reactive and loss components. The estimated expanded uncertainty is 6 muA/A at 1 MHz. Also level dependence of planar multijunction converters is reported.

articleTitle: A design and implementation of 3.5 mm coaxial microcalorimeter for RF and microwave power standards at KRISS
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: This paper describes the status of RF power standards at KRISS briefly and introduces the on going project which developing a 3.5 mm coaxial microcalorimeter for implementing the national power standard up to 26.5 GHz. Microcalorimeter design and developing process which based on CAD and computer aided engineering (CAE) will be discussed and some results will be shown.

articleTitle: Time domain antenna range at KRISS
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: We have fabricated 2.7 m long conical antenna range that is used in the characterization of UWB antenna in the time domain. The transfer function of the system was measured to be within 3 dB of the expected value, in the frequency range of 100 MHz to 18 GHz.

articleTitle: Precision inductance measurement on high precision capacitance bridge
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: For high precision impedance measurement only a very limited range of commercial instruments is available. The most accurate commercially available instruments for impedance measurements are capacitance bridges. Precise instruments for inductance or general impedance measurements are not available on the market. This paper describes novel methods for calibration of inductance reference standards from 1 muH to 10 kH using an accurate capacitance bridge with uncertainty on 1 kHz better than 50 ppm for 100 muH to 10 kH and better than 500 ppm for 1 muH and 10 muH. Main attention is paid to new measurement method using active or passive T-circuit for inductances from 1 muH to 1 H.

articleTitle: Development of an AC-DC transfer standard based on NbN/TiN/NbN programmable Josephson junction array
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: An ac-dc transfer measurement system based on a programmable Josephson voltage standard (PJVS) is being developed. Performance of the standard with dc and synthesized ac bias has been characterised. The first ac-dc transfer measurement results indicate agreement with conventional standards of the order of 1 muV/V at frequencies up to 40 Hz.

articleTitle: Progress on the LNE watt balance project
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: This paper describes the main progress on the LNE watt balance project since 2004. Development of different parts and structure of the watt balance including starting their assembly are presented.

articleTitle: Method for computing the effective aperture time in the HP3458
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: In this paper, the consequence of a difference between effective and programmed aperture time of the HP3458 is evaluated. The frequency response and the compensation is strongly frequency dependant, and is a function of aperture time. We show that deviation in aperture time leads to error in the compensation. We present a way to obtain the effective aperture time experimentally.

articleTitle: A sampling system based on Σ–Δ analog-to-digital converters
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: This paper describes advances in the hardware design of a system for characterizing and investigating high-resolution sigma-delta analog-to-digital converters. This work is being done in the frame of a Ph.D. study program in electrical engineering at the TU-BS, focusing the characterization and modeling of such converters with the help of sinusoidal and the PTB Josephson waveform synthesizers. An effective resolution of 18–19 bits at a sampling rate of 64 kHz has been attained.

articleTitle: Model for transient variation in stepwise synthesized Josephson sinewaves
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: This paper describes the influence of the bias current on transients when synthesizing an AC signal using a programmable Josephson voltage standard. Measured changes of the RMS value of synthesized signals are compared with the presented model.

articleTitle: Minimum phase response reconstruction of sampling oscilloscopes based on the NTN calibration
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: This paper describes an algorithm for determining the minimum phase response of sampling oscilloscopes of a linear time-invariant response function from its magnitude. The procedure is based on Kramers-Kronig relations in combination with the harmonic phase response measurement of the NTN calibration. Although the truncation of the Hilbert transform gives rise to large errors in estimated phase, these errors may be approximated by using three basis functions. As an example, we got the minimum-phase response reconstruction of sampling oscilloscopes in the frequency domain; its frequency resolution achieves 1 MHz.

articleTitle: On-line calibration of high voltage current transformers
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Calibration of current transformers, used in high voltage networks, is difficult to perform because conventional methods need to disconnect the transformer from the network, interrupting the electricity service for many hours. This is inconvenient and has high costs. In this paper, an alternative calibration method is proposed which does not need to interrupt the service. All measurements are done using the service current as excitation. No intervention is required on the high voltage transformer side. This proposal is also useful for current transformers used inside power transformers and generators, where it is very difficult to access to the primary circuit.

articleTitle: Effect of material properties on broadband electrical behavior of coplanar waveguides
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: We investigate the importance of broadband substrate permittivity and loss tangent data for accurately calculating the frequency-dependent characteristic impedance and propagation constant of ungrounded coplanar waveguides (CPWs). To determine the electrical properties of a CPW, we use a quasi-TEM model that takes into account the effects of non-ideal conductors, substrate loss and finite metallization thickness. The propagation of uncertainties is studied with the aid of Monte Carlo (MC) simulations.

articleTitle: Calibration for precision coaxial air lines in the frequency range up to 110 GHz
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: This paper summarizes about the evaluation process of precision coaxial air lines with 3.5 mm connectors. The mechanical measurements of the line’s diameters and length were made accurately using NMIJ’s standard original system. Some deformation has been observed in length of about 6.0 μm shortened and also in diameter due to connector fastening even with specified torque in the case of air lines with 3.5 mm connectors. NMIJ has established the reference standards of scattering parameters of coaxial lines with 1.0 mm connectors in the frequency range up to 110 GHz.

articleTitle: Comparison of CERN and metas high current standards up to 10kA
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: The Large Hadron Collider (LHC) particle accelerator project will require unprecedented accuracy in the control of the current to the superconducting magnets. A calibration infrastructure has been developed at CERN to ensure current measurement traceability to national standards. The traceability of CERN current measurement chain from 10 mA to 5 A has been assured by periodic calibrations at METAS but an inter- laboratory comparison was necessary to complete a "direct traceability loop" at the kA level. This paper presents the methods and the results of the comparison between CERN and METAS, up to currents of 10 kA.

articleTitle: A bilateral comparison of measurement of diameters and characteristic impedance of precision 3.5 mm coaxial air lines
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: This paper summaries a bilateral comparison of measurement of the diameters of two precision 3.5 mm coaxial air lines. These mechanical measurements were made independently by two national metrology institutes: NMIJ and NPL. The laboratories also calculated the characteristic impedances based on the measured diameter values. The difference between the characteristic impedances calculated by the two laboratories for both lines was less than 0.02 Ω. The uncertainty of this difference at a 95 % level of confidence, for each line, was 0.08 Ω and 0.31 Ω.

articleTitle: The Josephson effect based primary ac power standard at PTB: progress report
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: In its effort to continuously improve its capability for measuring active, reactive and apparent electrical power, the Physikalisch-Technische Bundesanstalt (PTB) has integrated a 10 V Josephson Waveform Synthesizer into its primary standard for electrical ac power. This direct link to a quantum standard provides direct traceability for the measurements by the digital sampler at the heart of the standard, besides reducing the uncertainty for measuring active, reactive and apparent power at the 600 VA apparent power level beyond the present level of 1.2 μW/VA (k = 1).

articleTitle: A measuring machine for the magnetic circuit of the LNE watt balance
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: This paper describes the measuring machine built to measure the direction of the axis of revolution of the magnetic field in the magnetic circuit of the LNE watt balance. It is also used to measure the air gap geometry and the flux density in the air gap.

articleTitle: Three-phase primary ac power sampling standard with improved frequency resolution
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: This paper describes the new PTB three-phase alternating (ac) power sampling standard. Based on two cascaded direct-digital-synthesizers, it allows calibrations with high frequency-resolution. The system is intended to reduce measurement uncertainties of three-phase power meter calibrations to less than 10 μW/VA and to alleviate staff’s daily burden of calibration routine.

articleTitle: A new sampling transfer standard of highest accuracy for AC quantities
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: The paper summarizes current efforts to develop a novel alternating (ac) sampling standard at the PTB in cooperation with ZERA- and EMH- GmbH in Germany. This instrument shall operate in the frequency range of 40 Hz to 5 kHz and serve as a transfer standard, allowing measurements with basic accuracies of some μV/V at 50 Hz to be made. It is intended to ensure improved traceability to the PTB primary standards of ac power and the PTB Josephson ac standard in calibration centers.

articleTitle: A high precision calibration setup for low-current meters in the range of 10 pA to 1 fA
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A low DC current source based on the method of charging a capacitor using a linear voltage ramp was built for the calibration of picoammeters and the metrological features of the setup were tested. The measurement uncertainty was improved by offset current compensation and a galvanic isolation between the personal computer and the ramp generator via opto-coupling. Using this setup, a low-current meter was calibrated in the range from 10 pA to 1 fA with an uncertainty of 3×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−5</sup> to 6×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−2</sup>.

articleTitle: Use of diffracted Gaussian beams in position sensing
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Authors present a novel method in position sensing based on the diffraction of Gaussian beams, their propagation properties and their spatial modulation . The idea is to focus two modulated and collimated Gaussian beams into a slit. The resulting diffracted beams at the slit illuminate a photodetector whose signal is demodulated by a lock-in amplifier. The response of the lock-in amplifier is a function of the slit position with respect to the two modulated Gaussian beams. Resolution of 25 pm can be achieved.

articleTitle: Error contributions in stepwise synthesized Josephson sine waves
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Synthesizing Josephson stepwise sine waves to produce an AC quantum standard is limited by errors in the waveform transitions between quantized voltages. Many parameters have an impact on the shape of the transients. In this paper, the effect from microwave power and the position of the ground connection on the array chip are discussed.

articleTitle: A measurement setup to calibrate picoammeters in dc current in the range 100 pA ÷100 nA
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: This paper describes a measurement setup for the calibration of pico-ammeters in dc current in the range 100 pA divide 100 nA. The system is based on a 100 MOmega Hamon network developed at INRIM to improve the traceability level of the maintained 1 GOmega standard. Besides the Hamon network, the measurement system consists of a precision dc voltage source and an electronic circuit used as voltage guard driver. A comparison with a different technique and an uncertainties considerations for the system and are also reported.

articleTitle: A simple technique for precision RF attenuation measurement
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: An accurate RF attenuation measurement, with small mismatch effect, is achieved without source and load being matched to the line impedance. Insertion loss measurements to the DUT and to the DUT fitted by quarter-wavelength lines are carried out, then the attenuation is obtained simply, unrelated to the source and load reflection coefficients. Experiment results on two 20-dB attenuators at 11 GHz show good agreements with those being impedance matched.

articleTitle: KRISS-NRC intercomparisons of calibration systems for instrument transformers with many different ratios at power frequency
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: An intercomparison of calibration systems for instrument transformers between Korea Research Institute of Standards and Science (KRISS) and National Research Council of Canada (NRC) with many different ratios at 60 Hz was performed using six portable transfer standards consisting of two current transformers (CTs) with current ratios of 5 A/5 A up to 20,000 A/5 A and four voltage transformers (VTs) with voltage ratios of 110 V/110 V up to 66,000 V/110 V. The comparison results for the instrument transformers calibration systems between the two institutes are in good agreement within the corresponding expanded uncertainties for all current and voltage ratios.

articleTitle: Uncertainty evaluation in a two-terminal cryogenic current comparator
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: In this paper we present the uncertainty evaluation of a new cryogenic current comparator (CCC) bridge designed to compare two-terminal 1 MOmega and 10 MOmega standard resistors with the quantized Hall resistance (QHR) and then scale from these values to other values between 10 kOmega and 1 GOmega.

articleTitle: Towards a final result from the NPL Mark II watt balance
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: The NPL Mk II watt balance made an initial series of measurements of Planck's constant in the period from October 2006 to March 2007. The results of these measurements differ significantly from those recently published by NIST. Watt balance research at NPL is continuing until March 2008 aiming to reduce the uncertainty associated with the NPL measurement and to further investigate possible sources of the difference.

articleTitle: Reproducibility of the metas watt balance
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: After several mechanical improvements, the METAS watt balance has been fully operational during the last 18 months. The reproducibility, alignment issues and the long term stability of the apparatus are discussed.

articleTitle: Improvement in the volume determination for Si spheres with an optical interferometer
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Accurate volume measurements for silicon spheres by optical interferometers play an important role in the determination of the Avogadro constant by the X-ray crystal density method. To reduce the uncertainty in the volume determination, a new vacuum chamber with a radiation shield has been developed. A new sphere temperature measurement system has been also introduced. Details of the improvements are described.

articleTitle: New TWSTFT link between LNE-SYRTE and NTSC in the Ku band
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: We report first results obtained with the Two Way Satellite Time and Frequency Transfer (TWSTFT) between LNE-SYRTE and NTSC using the IS-4 commercial geostationary satellite at 72<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sup> E operating in Ku band. This work is part of the activities recommended by the CCTF working group on TWSTFT. The detailed study of the measurement uncertainty is presented, with particular attention to the fluctuation of Sagnac effect due to the satellite libration.

articleTitle: 10 volt Josephson series array voltage standard at NPL, India
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Josephson series array voltage standard at 10 volt level has been recently established at National Physical Laboratory (NPL), India. This paper describes the measurement set up and the results that have been obtained in calibrating the secondary standard.

articleTitle: On-site calibration of a current transformer using a Rogowski coil
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: This paper describes an outdoor calibration of an instrument current transformer connected to 400 kV transmission line. The method of generation of the high current and the accuracy of calibration are discussed. The reference current measuring system consists of a current shunt, a Rogowski coil, two digitizing voltmeters and a computer to control voltmeters. The Rogowski coil is calibrated on-site with the current shunt. The output voltage of the Rogowski coil is not integrated, but it is scaled according to the on-site calibration result. Estimated uncertainties for ratio and phase displacement are less than 0,01% and 100 murad, respectively.

articleTitle: Direct comparisons of ac resistance standards of various technology designs
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: In this paper, we present results of direct AC resistance comparisons carried out at LNE with a four terminal-pair coaxial impedance bridge in 1:1 and 10:1 ratios at frequencies up to 1.6 kHz. Various ac calculable resistance standards have been used, having 1 kOmega and 10 kOmega nominal values and different technology designs. LNE standards were a coaxial straight wire resistor of Haddad type and two thin film coaxial resistors, while MIKES standards were two folded wire bifilar resistors. The whole changes in frequency of the resistance ratios are within some parts in 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">8</sup>.

articleTitle: Development of a voltage divider based on quantized Hall resistance arrays for a high DC voltage standard II
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A one-chip quantized voltage divider device based on the technology of integration of quantized Hall resistance (QHR) bars on a GaAs/AlGaAs heterostructure substrate has been developed. The first experimental QHR voltage divider device, which consists of a series of 20 QHR bars, has been fabricated. A preliminary test in our evaluation study of the device clearly shows that it functions as a voltage multiplier/divider.

articleTitle: Calibration of high-voltage current-comparator-based capacitance and dissipation factor bridges using nonsynchronous digital sampling
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A new calibration system for automated high-voltage current-comparator-based capacitance and dissipation factor bridges is presented. It does not require synchronization circuits between the digitizers and the generators. It is possible to simulate 1:1 capacitance ratio and dissipation factors from 1<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">.</sup>10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-6</sup> with standard uncertainties of less than to 1<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">.</sup>10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> with standard uncertainties of less than 1<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">.</sup>10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-5</sup>.

articleTitle: Novel digital voltage ramp generator for picoammeter calibrations
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: For the calibration of picoammeters a novel highly linear voltage ramp generator has been constructed which is based on digital electronics and two digital-to-analog-converters (DACs). In contrast to our previous ramp generator constructed entirely in analog electronics the new design allows for the first time to perform dynamic measurements without any sacrifice of linearity.

articleTitle: A simple impedance correction for on-wafer TAN calibration techniques
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A general method initially developed for the estimation of the S-parameters measurement errors caused by non-ideal calibration standards, is applied for the correction of the reference impedance of 7- term through-attenuator-network (TAN) calibration procedures such as thru-attenuator reflect (TAR). Deviations from ideal calibration elements are measured on-wafer using the multiline TRL method and can be taken into account without the need for a precise determination of the reference impedance (lumped elements).

articleTitle: Calibration of a 3.5 mm coaxial power sensor using a transfer standard with 7 mm coaxial or WR42 waveguide connectors
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A calibration system of a 3.5 mm coaxial power sensor was implemented using transfer standards with 7 mm coaxial or K-band waveguide input connectors. A 7 mm-3.5 mm or WR42-3.5 mm adapter was used to form a combined transfer standard. The effective efficiency of the combined transfer standard was obtained. The 3.5 mm coaxial power sensor was calibrated using the well-known direct comparison method and measurement uncertainty was evaluated.

articleTitle: Setup of shot noise measurement in a tunnel junction for noise thermometry
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: We report our development of a low-temperature shot noise measurement set-up for noise thermometry. We have constructed an experimental set-up for measuring shot noise in the frequency range of 700-1000 MHz. We have fabricated metallic tunnel-junction devices consisting of Al-AlO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub>-Al by two angle-evaporation method. The current-voltage characteristic of the tunnel junction showed an ohmic behavior up to bias voltage of ~3k<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">B</sub>T/e at room temperature. Also, the characteristics of RF components including RF amplifiers, circulators, directional couplers were investigated.

articleTitle: Atomic layer deposited alumina (Al2O3) coating on thin film cryoresistors
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Metal alloy (NiCrCuAlGe) thin film resistors were coated with atomic layer deposited (ALD) alumina (Al<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>) in order to improve the stability and repeatability of the high value resistors (100 kOmega - 500 kOmega) in the temperature range from 4.2 K to 300 K. The drift rate of the resistance due to the native oxidation at room temperature was reduced from -2.45 ppm/h for an uncoated resistor to 0.03 ppm/h for an alumina-coated resistor. It was shown that the additional alumina coating does not significantly change the thermoelectrical properties of the metal alloy thin film resistors.

articleTitle: CCEM-K10 key comparison of resistance standards at 100 Ω
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A key comparison of resistance standards at 100 Omega started in 2001. The pilot laboratory, seven national metrological institutes, and the BIPM participated in that comparison. The results of this comparison are reported.

articleTitle: A voltage source for low frequency AC waveforms with quantum traceability to a Josephson array reference using sampling and feedback
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: We describe a method for generating a low frequency sinusoidal calibration voltage with reference to a quantum standard, at the point of connection to the instrument under test (DUT). The voltage is made traceable to the maintained SI unit by a sampling system that compares the applied potential difference to that developed by an array of Josephson junctions. A feedback loop allows the use of a silicon DAC and active filter to source the current necessary to establish the potential difference, whilst maintaining quantum-derived accuracy with an uncertainty less than 1 muV per volt.

articleTitle: Calibration methods for electrostatic discharge generators
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: This paper describes a calibration set-up for electrostatic discharge (ESD) generators used in electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) immunity tests. A coaxial shunt and a voltage divider are used for current and voltage measurements respectively. The presented measuring systems are traceable to the national standards.

articleTitle: Frequency calibration based on adaptive neural-fuzzy inference system
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A new scheme of frequency calibration based on adaptive neural-fuzzy inference system (ANFIS) is proposed in this paper. In normal mode, an oven-controlled crystal oscillator (OCXO) is steered by integrating time interval counter (TIC), fuzzy controller, D/A converter, etc., such that its frequency can follow a primary cesium atomic clock. In addition, the ANFIS is applied when the system enters holdover mode. Experimental results show that the frequency stability of the OCXO can be improved from a few parts in 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">9</sup> to 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">13</sup> for averaging times of one day, as well as the performance could be maintained within a few parts in 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</sup> over one day in the holdover mode.

articleTitle: The ac quantum Hall effect: About gates and image charges
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: We report some new results and insights about the effect of back-gates, side-gates, and image charges on the ac properties of the quantum Hall effect.

articleTitle: Next-generation calculable capacitor using a tunable-laser interferometer
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A new calculable capacitor with an operating range of 0.1 pF is being developed at NIST. Incorporation of Fabry-Perot displacement metrology employing a tunable laser will allow a continuous set of electrode displacements, as opposed to the discrete set in the current implementation. In addition, the reduced uncertainty in the displacement measurement will allow a considerably more compact apparatus, greatly minimizing errors arising from other sources.

articleTitle: Mass determination with the magnetic levitation method
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: The project for the realisation of the kilogram using the ldquosuperconducting magnetic levitation methodrdquo has been continued at MIKES. From the results of the subproject, calorimetric measurements, we have come to the conclusion that the realisation of the kilogram based on the levitation method is difficult with the present knowledge of energy losses in superconductors due to incomplete Meissner effect. New materials or measurement methods has to be found. A new improved test system under the consideration will be presented.

articleTitle: Generic implementation of Monte Carlo method for uncertainty evaluation. Application to calibration of RF power sensors
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: The ISO GUM provides a framework for uncertainty evaluation using the law of propagation of uncertainty (GUF). The output quantity is characterized by a Gaussian or student-t distribution. Supplement one to the GUM deals with the propagation of probability distributions of the input quantities of a mathematical model of measurement for the evaluation of uncertainty by a Monte Carlo method. This paper gives an overview of the application of this method and integration with an automated software calibration. The method is applied to power sensors calibration, and results are used to validate the applicability of GUF.

articleTitle: Generation of two coherent laser sources selected from femtosecond laser frequency comb and resonant two-photon spectroscopy of Cesium atoms
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Experimental setup We report on a generation of two coherent continuous wave (cw) laser sources with a wavelength difference of 57 nm based on a femtosecond laser frequency comb (FLFC) injection locked diode lasers. The FLFC wavelength near 852 nm is optically injected to the DBR diode laser, and the other DFB diode laser is injection locked by a FCFL at near 794 nm. Two diode lasers are independently injection locked by two different mode of one FLFC. Therefore, two diode lasers are phase-coherent because it is well known that individual mode of a FLFC are phase-coherent each other. We demonstrate the resonant two-photon spectroscopy of 6S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1/2</sub>-6P<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3/2</sub>-8S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1/2</sub> transition line for the Cesium atom by using two injection locked diode lasers.

articleTitle: Calibration of four-terminal-pair resistor
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Based on the standard capacitor acting as reference standard from 100 kHz to 10 MHz, the measurement principle of four-terminal-pair impedance and the open-short-load (OSL) technique are used to calibrate the frequency characteristic of four-terminal pair resistor. In order to eliminate or reduce the nonlinearity error of measurement instrument, the method can keep measurement range of instrument invariable by selecting different nominal standard capacitor at the different calibration frequency.

articleTitle: Simultaneous comparison of impedance standards by means of commercial digital LCR-meters
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Application of ratio voltage or current transformers allows to use commercial digital LCR-meter as a comparator of two impedances. Advantages of such comparison method include the opportunity to increase the resolution up to 7–8 digits and the elimination of an error from nonlinearity of a meter.

articleTitle: Atmospheric pressure sensitivity of the ultrastable monolithic nonplanar ring lasers
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Atmospheric pressure sensitivity of the ultrastable monolithic nonplanar ring laser has been observed in optic frequency standard experiments. Atmospheric pressure perturbations affect the frequency stability of monolithic nonplanar ring lasers about 3.7 GHz/kPa. In this paper, this susceptibility is measured and quantitatively analyzed. This phenomenon needs to be cancelled in portable device of the 532-nm I<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>-stabilized optical frequency standards.

articleTitle: A new power converter for active, reactive and apparent power at power frequencies
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A compact, highly accurate and stable power converter has been developed at PTB to improve future comparisons of electric alternating power. It is particularly suitable for sinusoidal input signals of 120 V or 60 V and 5 A or 1 A at power frequencies for any value of their power factor.

articleTitle: Prototype of a pendulum for deriving the kilogram from electrical quantities
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: This paper describes a prototype of a pendulum for deriving the kilogram from the electrical quantities. The equivalent inertial mass of the pendulum is derived from the measurement of the position of the moving assembly and the electrical quantities (electromotive force and current) on a coil as a function of time. The prototype shows the functionality of the method, identifying the operative limits for an implementation aimed at measurement at metrological level.

articleTitle: CCC Bridge with digitally-controlled current sources
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: We have built a CCC resistance bridge for the comparison of standard resistors in the range from 1 Omega to 100 kOmega. The use of fully programmable current sources allows for smooth polarity reversals, regardless of the time constant of each side of the bridge. The CCC has a transfer function of 2.25 muA/phi<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> and a measured noise level of 54 pAldrturn/radic(Hz) at 1 Hz.

articleTitle: An electrochemical cell for the Faraday constant determination
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A new 2-electrode cell for the electro-gravimetric determination of silver has been designed and is now under test. The new set-up allows accurate galvanostatic measurements of the dissolution of the Ag electrode with a strict control on the Ag<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup> ion concentration in the two sides of the cell solution. The solution stability, the residue recovery, the O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> prevention and the solution filtering process without its transfer in other containers are other merits. This cell will be employed for the measurement of the Faraday constant.

articleTitle: Oxide layer mass determination at the silicon sphere of the Avogadro Project
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Within the International Avogadro Project two spheres of highly enriched <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">28</sup>Si crystals have been produced, to perform a new determination of the Avogadro constant N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">A</sub>. As one of the critical tasks the mass of the oxide layer of the spheres has to be measured.

articleTitle: Systematic errors in shot noise thermometer measurements
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: We report comparisons between the Shot Noise Thermometer (SNT), a primary thermometer based on the electronic noise from a tunnel junction, and the ITS-90 in the temperature range from 4 K to 30 K. The SNT indicates a temperature that is systematically high compared to T<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">90</sub>, and we explain the probable origin of this effect. We characterize other systematic effects in the SNT and provide a roadmap for future extensions in the accuracy of the SNT which could make it metrologically useful in the lower-most ranges of the ITS-90 and especially in the range of the PLTS-2000.

articleTitle: Calibration of horizontally-placed planarity standards
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Fused silica plates are used in most metrology laboratories as planarity standard. Usually, these standards are calibrated in upright position, to minimize bending effects due to gravity. On the other hand, for particular applications or very large flats, it would be useful to know the absolute surface error when they are supported in horizontal position, i.e., with their axis vertical. Here we report a study regarding this setup for planarity calibration, comparing two different experimental methods with respect to predictions of finite elements analysis.

articleTitle: VNIIM-NRC intercomparison of calibration systems for large value capacitors up to 10 μF at frequencies up to 1 kHz
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A number of international comparisons of calibration systems for capacitors up to 1 nF were conducted in the past at frequencies about 1000 Hz. This intercomparison of large value capacitors calibration systems between VNIIM and NRC was done at frequencies of 50 Hz, 60 Hz, and 1000 Hz. The comparison was implemented with a set of transfer standards, developed by VNIIM, with nominal capacitance values (nF) of 1, 10, 100, 1000, and 10,000. The comparison results, including the transfer standard and calibration systems at VNIIM and NRC, will be presented.

articleTitle: Traceable Johnson noise measurements in the audio frequency range
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A simple setup for the accurate measurement of Johnson noise of a resistor is here presented. The setup is composed of a digital correlation spectrum analyzer, and of a calibration signal source traceable to ac voltage and frequency standards. If resistor temperature is measured, an estimate of the Boltzmann constant k<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">B</sub> can be obtained. Presently, measured k<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">B</sub> has a relative error below 1times10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-3</sup> with respect to the accepted value.

articleTitle: Phase control of microwave oscillators using an optical clock laser as reference
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: This paper describes the improvement of the stability of a low phase noise microwave source at 9.6 GHz using a fiber-based fs-frequency-comb and an optical reference frequency. We show that the stability of the optical clock can be transferred to the microwave domain without tight locking of the frequency comb.

articleTitle: Frequency stability characterisation of a strontium trapped ion optical frequency standard
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Two 674-nm optical frequency standards based on the <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1/2</sub> - <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>D<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5/2</sub> transition in <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">88</sup>Sr<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup> are under development at NPL. Comparison of the standards allows determination of the frequency stability and reproducibility via difference frequency measurements. A relative frequency stability between the traps of ap3times10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-15</sup> over a 100 s averaging time has been observed. A compact, transportable system is also being developed, which could find application in ground stations or as an optical frequency clock in space.

articleTitle: 3-D field simulation to design a calculable capacitor
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Investigation of an electrode system for a new calculable capacitor is being carried out at NIST through 3-D field simulation.
