From the results, we have determined the most critical factors to the design of the system. The scope of the study would not have been possible through any empirical study.

articleTitle: Universality of the quantized Hall resistance
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: The discovery of the quantum Hall effect (QHE) in 1980 by Klaus von Klitzing has revolutionized the resistance metrology. Today, the quantized Hall resistance (QHR), observed in a two-dimensional electron gas exposed to a high magnetic flux at low temperatures, is used worldwide as an invariant reference for electrical calibrations. It has improved the reproducibility of calibration results by up to two orders of magnitude during the last two decades. The best resistance bridges such as the cryogenic current comparator or the Josephson potentiometer allow the comparison of the QHR with conventional resistance standards at a level of a few parts in 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</sup>.

articleTitle: Absorption line profile measurement of rovibrational transition of acetylene molecule using a fiber comb spectrometer
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: We have been developing a spectrometer to record an accurate absorption line profile of a rovibrational transition of acetylene in the 1.54 mum region using an extended cavity laser diode (ECLD) and a mode-locked fiber frequency comb. With the spectrometer, we have recorded the absorption line profiles for various pressures and have observed the collisional narrowing effect on the inhomogeneous Gaussian widths. Information of the Gaussian width which reflects the Maxwell-Boltzmann distribution can be used to estimate accurate temperature of the sample gas and also have possibility to provide a way to determine the Boltzmann constant.

articleTitle: Measurement of neutron binding energy of 36Cl for a determination of NAh
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Precise wave length measurements of gamma rays emitted after thermal neutron capture reaction allow the determination of the neutron’s binding energy within a nucleus. Comparing this energy to atomic mass measurements gives direct access to the molar Planck constant N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">A</inf>h. This result will be of utmost importance in the context of a re-definition of the kilogram via the Planck and the Avogadro constants. Having this in mind, any future measurement must yield a relative uncertainty of better then 5×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−8</sup>. An essential step towards this goal is to demonstrate that there are no statistical limitations for such an experiment. In the present contribution we report on the results of the recently performed binding energy measurement on <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">36</sup>Cl using a modified version of the double flat crystal spectrometer GAMS4.

articleTitle: Clock laser system for strontium lattice clock
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: We report on the setup and characterization of a 698 nm master-slave diode laser system to probe the <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>-<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> clock transition of strontium atoms confined in a 1D optical lattice. The instability and the line-width of the laser system have been measured with respect to an ultrastable 657 nm diode laser with 1 Hz linewidth [1] utilizing the transfer oscillator principle [2] with a femtosecond fiber comb. The magnetic-field-induced clock transition of <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">88</sup>Sr can be used to investigate the instability of the 698 nm clock laser system at intermediate averaging times.

articleTitle: The equivalent circuit of air capacitor in high frequency range
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: The air capacitor has a very good frequency response and is suitable to act as an impedance standard for the frequency range of several MHz. In this paper, the determination of capacitance at high frequency is discussed. It should be noted that the result depends on the form of equivalent circuit used. An ordinary simple circuit of lumped parameters gives an inaccurate result and a distributed parameter circuit gives a better result for capacitance at high frequency. This work is important when an air capacitor is intended for use as an a reference standard.

articleTitle: Analysis of measurement comparison EUROMET.EM-K2
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: This paper describes the analysis of a measurement comparison of resistance standards, using a method of constrained least squares. The approach is based on [1] which provides a general framework for the analysis of measurement comparisons independent of their complexity.

articleTitle: Free space antenna factor of a dipole antenna and uncertainty from 1 to 2 GHz
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Free space dipole antenna factor above 1 GHz and associated uncertainty are presented. Theoretical site insertion loss containing the antenna alignment and terminal impedances is given for the uncertainty analysis. Antenna factors are obtained with uncertainty of 0.4 dB in the entire frequency range.

articleTitle: Electrostatic actuated mems for precision AC voltage references
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: The purpose of this paper is to present results on the design of electrostatic actuated micro- electromechanical systems (MEMS) aiming at developing AC voltage references through mechanical-electrical transduction for electrical metrology and more generally for miniaturized instrumentation. Several test MEMS architectures (targeted AC voltages from 10 V up to 100 V) for the vertical motion have been designed and are under fabrication by an epitaxial silicon on insulator (SOI) surface micromachining process with the aim to investigate the potentialities of the different structures with respect to the geometrical dispersion, the strain sensitivity and the electrical stability.

articleTitle: Terminal tightness: Improving the stability of a four-terminal standard resistor
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: The four-terminal resistance of commonly used Tinsley Type 5685A 100 Omega resistors can vary significantly depending upon how firmly the terminals are tightened. Our measurements show a resistance to change of 12 nOmega/Omega for one resistor to an extreme case of 8000 nOmega/Omega for another resistor for which the body of one current terminal could rotate relatively easily. These findings makes it necessary to exercise care when connecting and reconnecting these resistors and also necessary to develop a way of effectively detecting or better still preventing terminal body rotation.

articleTitle: Measuring the gravitational constant with a cryogenic torsion pendulum
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Concluding results from an extensive program to measure the gravitational constant G will be presented. Data were obtained from y2000 to 2006 using a torsion pendulum in the 'dynamic' ("time-of-swing") mode, operating at temperatures ~2.7 K. Six torsion fibers of three types were used with torsional oscillation amplitudes between 0.3 and 7.4 radians: BeCu as-drawn, BeCu heat treated, and Al5056 as-drawn. A metrology scale factor is hidden until data and metrology analysis are complete, to minimize danger of experimenter bias. Some evidence for both amplitude and fiber material dependence is found which is expected to limit our uncertainty to about 50 ppm. A final G value will be reported at CPEM2008.

articleTitle: Injection locked DFB laser as an optical frequency reference in the infrared region based on femtosecond fiber laser comb
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: We demonstrate a DFB laser that can be injection locked to desire single mode of a femtosecond fiber laser comb. The femtosecond injection locking technique that can select one component among the fiber laser comb modes was applied to the comb selection. The DFB laser injection locked to the desired comb mode was used as optical frequency reference for absolute frequency measurement of an acetylene stabilized laser. The absolute frequency of the laser stabilized on the P(16) transition of <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">13</sup>C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> was estimated to be 194 369 569 385.7 kHz.

articleTitle: Design and fabrication of MJTCs on quartz substrates at NIST
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Dry etching is employed in the fabrication of new planar, thin-film multijunction thermal converters (MJTCs) on quartz membranes and crystalline quartz chips at NIST. The use of crystalline quartz as a material for the membrane and for the chip improves the performance of the MJTC in the frequency range from 100 kHz to 100 MHz. Simulations of the ac-dc voltage transfer difference for a heater resistance of 400 Omega in the frequency range from 1 MHz to 100 MHz show a reduction in the ac-dc transfer difference of more than one order of magnitude in comparison with MJTCs fabricated on silicon chips.

articleTitle: The determinations of the Boltzmann constant
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: The international community started recently to look for a new way to define the Kelvin. Different experiments around the world have begun. This presentation will describe very briefly the four different techniques currently used for the redetermination of k, namely the measurement of the speed of sound in pure helium-4, the determination deduce of the Doppler profile of the linear absorption line, the measurement of the noise power in an electrical resistance and finally the change of refractive index in function of the density of pure helium-4.

articleTitle: Precision ac-dc transfer measurement system based on a 1000-volt inductive voltage divider
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: The paper presents a new AC-DC transfer measurement system for voltages up to 1000 V and frequencies up to 1 kHz based on a precision inductive voltage divider. Preliminary evaluations show the possibility of standard uncertainties of less than 3 muV/V at 1000 V.

articleTitle: Josephson voltage standard locked sinewaves synthesizer
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: This paper describes a Josephson voltage standard locked synthesizer where a commercial digital to analog converter is used as a sine wave generator whose output is controlled (in phase and amplitude) by the calculable fundamental of the stepwise sinuisoidal wave generated by a SINIS array. Such a system combines the versatility of a commercial source with the stability and accuracy of the Josephson standard.

articleTitle: Exchange of the 10 V Josephson array chip in the SMU voltage standard
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Interlaboratory comparison of the SMU 10 V Josephson array voltage standard (JAVS) has been carried out with the CMI JAVS. The comparison method was indirect using Zener diode reference as the traveling standard. This paper presents besides the results of the comparison that the parameters of the SMU primary standard have been preserved after the exchange of the Josephson array chip in the system. The results show agreement between the SMU and the CMI calibrations of the Fluke 732 B reference standard 280 nV.

articleTitle: Improving the primary power standard below 10 MHz with thermoelectric sensors
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: High frequency power standard is quite everywhere implemented using the microcalorimeter technique. At INRiM a twin type coaxial microcalorimeter is used to measure the effective efficiency of thermoelectric detectors from direct current up to 40 GHz. However, below 10 MHz there is a lack of sensitivity that reduces the power standard accuracy. To work around the problem, we propose to calibrate the power detectors trough RF voltage measurements in the lowest frequency band.

articleTitle: Secondary standard of AC voltage scale transformation coefficient unit at primary rated voltages of 400/ √3 and 500/ √3 kV
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Developed and approved in 2007 Secondary Standard of AC voltage scale transformation coefficient (VSTC) unit at primary rated voltages of 400 / radic3 kV and 500 / radic3 kV is described below.

articleTitle: Progress on the BIPM watt balance
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Since the beginning of the development in spring 2005, considerable progress has been made on the BIPM watt balance. We have continued the development of a room temperature experiment to test the feasibility of simultaneous force and velocity measurements. We are now able to simultaneously acquire the velocity and voltage of the moving coil and to deduce their ratio. This article briefly recalls the main ideas of the BIPM watt balance and reports the progress to date and the preliminary results.

articleTitle: The thermal model building and calculation of portable air enclosure
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: This paper describes our specially designed portable air enclosure for preserving the calculable AC transferring resistor. The inner space of enclosure is 300mm×250mm×300mm. Through solving the Laplace equation of heat conduction in sphere region a worthy conclusion is obtained: When the dimension of the layer of temperature homogeneity approaches the geometrical mean of size of the layer of thermal insulation and inner chamber, the inner temperature homogeneity of portable air enclosure is optimal.

articleTitle: Power bridge based on current transformer for enlarging measurement frequency range up to 10kHz
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: There are a lot of advantages in a power bridge using a current comparator, such as for can be the structure concise, the limitation of the number of error factors etc. However, a small problem might be left about a point how carry out the calibration of the comparator. This problem is settled immediately if the comparator could be replaced with a current transformer. Therefore it is assumed that the current comparator is placed as the primary standard and the CT is an instrument of under-test in a traceability style. Because the uncertainty of the CT does not exceed the comparator, the uncertainty of the power bridge in which the CT installed replaced by the comparator will be inferior more than traditional power bridge. However, the current transformer is a standard that is necessary and is indispensable to the electric power and energy measurement system, and it is easy to become familiar the traceability. In addition, it is expected that the width of the design that specializes in the performances such as reducing the error or expanding the frequency response extends, and the evaluation of the uncertainty for the power standard is simplified if the CT utilized in the power bridge. We propose the use of the CT for the power bridge with no burden.

articleTitle: Development of thin film range resistors for high-voltage AC-DC transfer standards
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: New thin-film range resistors have been developed at the National Metrology Institute of Japan (NMIJ) to reduce the voltage dependence of AC-DC transfer differences that have appeared in the processes of the step-up procedures over 300 V. The occurrence of voltage dependence is partly due to rising ambience temperature that may cause changes in the resistance of the resistor and the temperature dependence of the dielectric losses in the coating of the resistor. In order to avoid these problems, our new thin film heaters were directly sputtered on an AlN substrate and covered with SiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> film. The material of the heater is a NiCrFeAl alloy, which has a low temperature coefficient of the resistor around room temperature. This paper describes the reduction of the voltage dependence of AC-DC transfer differences over 300 V by improving the design of the range resistors for high-voltage thermal voltage converters (TVCs).

articleTitle: Cryogen-free operation of programmable Josephson voltage standard with a closed-cycle refrigerator
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: We report operation of a programmable Josephson voltage standard on a closed-cycle refrigerator. NIST 1V PJVS chip is used, and we operate the chip with the fingerboard that is adopted from the existing liquid helium dipping probe. We demonstrate operation at 5.5 K of chip temperature, with a flat Shapiro step in the sub-array of the chip.

articleTitle: Permittvity and permeability and the basis of effective parameters
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: The concepts of effective permittivity and permeability are used throughout the literature to describe heterogeneous materials, inhomogeneous materials, and small collections of molecules. In this paper we study definitions of the permittivity and permeability based on the microscopic Maxwell's equations and then discuss the ramifications of the common usage of the term "effective".

articleTitle: Two advanced approaches for a semi-automatic, octave-spanning optical frequency counter
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: This paper demonstrates two approaches to determine the absolute mode number of the comb line for a semi-automatic optical frequency counter based on two mode-locked fiber laser combs. In the first approach, two laser combs were operated at three different repetition rates with two of them are so close to each other that their beating mode numbers are the same. In the second approach, the laser combs were operated at two different repetition rate and monochromators were used to offer an approximate mode number to determine the exact mode number from the two measured beat frequencies.

articleTitle: Strontium optical lattice clock with high accuracy and stability
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Techniques of modern quantum optics allows for the preparation of atoms in well controlled quantum states ideal for precision measurements and tests of fundamental laws of physics. We report on our recent progress with a highly stable and accurate optical atomic clock based on ultracold fermionic <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">87</sup>Sr atoms confined in a one dimensional optical lattice. Currently, we have carried out a detailed evaluation of our clock at the 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−16</sup> level and can report stability at 2 x 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−15</sup> level at one second. At typical operating parameters for the clock we observe evidence of a density dependent clock shift. Operating the clock at a particular excitation ratio of ground state and excited clock state we observe a shift consistent with zero.

articleTitle: Phase extraction method based on real wavelet transform
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Phase information (PI) is important. Complex wavelet transform (CoWT)-based PI extraction methods are popular. Real discrete wavelet transform (RDWT) is simple, fast and non-redundant, but it is usually regarded to be lack of PI. This paper presented three RDWT-based PI extraction methods and proved these methods are equal to CoWT-based ones. Demonstration examples are given.

articleTitle: A survey of Josephson comparisons
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: In 2007 the CCEM proposed changes in the SI electrical units (Recommendation E-1), which has refocused attention on the validity and accuracy of the Josephson effect. We review comparisons of Josephson effect voltage standards and summarize the results as they pertain to the accuracy of the Josephson relationship between voltage and frequency. We also report a list of possible influence parameters and the range and accuracy over which they have been evaluated.

articleTitle: Study on the calibration of partial discharge calibrator
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: The calibration of apparent charge, which can be traced to AC voltage and capacitance, for partial discharge(PD) calibrator is discussed. The methods of fast sampling measurement of peak-to-peak amplitude for step voltage by digital multimeter and the arithmetic in the automatic measurement of apparent charge by digital oscilloscope are focused on. Then, other factors, such as impulse waveform and the choice of capacitor are also discussed.

articleTitle: Low leakage noise filter for direct comparison of two Josephson junction arrays in 102212;10 uncertainty level
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: High insulation low pass filters (LPFs) are often useful to improve the step stability of the Josephson array. However ordinarily available capacitors of high insulation at DC usually show a large transient leakage effect when the polarity of input voltage is reversed. A low leakage LPF with polarity reverse switch was made to reduce the transient leakage effect. The characteristics and its effect on the accuracy are evaluated using two Josephson arrays as voltage sources.

articleTitle: Improved Monte Carlo uncertainty modelling with cross-frequency correlation for microwave dielectric reference liquid data
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Published RF and microwave data on dielectric reference liquids [NPL Report CETM33] are reassessed to allow quoted measurement uncertainties to be reduced. The aim is to make the data maximally useful to users. The modelling approach followed should have application beyond dielectric metrology.

articleTitle: International comparison on ac-dc current transfer standards at frequencies up to 1 MHz
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: The paper presents an international comparison of ac-dc current transfer measurements at 10 mA and frequencies up to 1 MHz. The standards of NMIA, PTB and BEV have already been compared. The comparison is currently being extended to involve SP. The results will be presented at the conference.

articleTitle: Stepwise waveform synthesis using a programmable Josephson junction array
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A waveform synthesizer adopting a programmable Josephson voltage standard has been developed, which can produce stepwise sinusoidal waveforms with few hundred quantum voltage levels. For synthesis of waveforms, individual cells on the Josephson array chip were promptly biased using a 7-channel current source with 14-bit resolution. As an application, the synthesizer was utilized as a fast-reversed DC voltage source in evaluating the thermoelectric transfer difference for a thermal voltage converter.

articleTitle: Optical frequency comb comparison between optical clock configuration and optical frequency synthesizer
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: We report on accuracy test results on the comparison of two different types of optical frequency combs, each of those referenced to a microwave frequency standard and an optical frequency standard. One of those combs is based on a mode-locked erbium-doped fiber laser and the other is based on a Ti:sapphire femtosecond laser. The comb comparison was carried out by measuring an absolute frequency of an acetylene-stabilized diode laser with both combs simultaneously.

articleTitle: Density of a single crystal natural silicon sphere
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: The density of the single crystal natural silicon sphere Avo#3 has been re-determined at the National Measurement Institute, Australia (NMIA) as part of an international collaboration to determine the value of the Avogadro constant. A systematic review of the measurement system found a significant bias was introduced by the response of the laser to frequency steps during phase-shifting interferometry, which was characterized and corrected for. The density reported is based on new and re-calculated measurements taken between April 2000 and May 2006 during the ongoing development of the measurement system.

articleTitle: Cesium 6S1/2→8S1/2 two photon-transition stabilized 822.5nm diode laser
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: We construct a frequency stabilized extended-cavity diode laser (ECDL) at 822.5 nm wavelength that could be a reliable frequency reference. The laser frequency is locked to the Cs 6S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1/2</sub>rarr8S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1/2</sub> two-photon-transition (TPT) with the Allan deviation of 4.4times10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-13</sup> (60 s). The possible systematic error is evaluated as 2 kHz.

articleTitle: An iodine-stabilized Yb:YAG laser
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A monolithic-ring-cavity Yb:YAG laser is frequency doubled and used to perform Doppler-free spectroscopy of molecular iodine at 515 nm. The Allan standard deviation of the iodine-stabilized Yb:YAG laser is better than 6.2×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−14</sup> for a 10-s averaging time, which is limited by the stability of the H-maser involved in the frequency measurement using an optical comb.

articleTitle: Absolute frequency measurement of 40Ca+ in a Paul trap
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: We report on an absolute frequency measurement of a single <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">40</sup>Ca<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup> ion in a linear Paul trap at the 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-15</sup> level. A Cs-referenced frequency comb is used to measure the probe laser exciting the 4s<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1/2</sub> to 3d<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>D<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5/2</sub> quadrupole transition at 411 THz. A careful analysis of the estimated systematic shifts is given as well as an outlook on possible improvements.

articleTitle: The research of internet-enabled calibrating equipment for AC electrical energy meters
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: The workload of calibrating equipment for AC electrical energy meters is getting more and more heavy. One subject is put forwarded which is using internet to carry on long-distance calibration. The system's designing theory, testing procedure, utilization of software and hardware hanged together are described particularly in this paper.

articleTitle: Application of counter Helmholtz’s coils in the magneto optical trap
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: In this paper, theoretical calculation to related parameter of the counter-Helmholtz's coils is first processed, and experimentalized it later. It was found that time constant T is always fell short of destined target. Think over winding parameter and the correlative theoretical calculation is processed. Additionally, we improved experimental testing set. Here, the measured time constant is accorded with destined target, viz. T<1 ms.

articleTitle: Setting up a binary system for synthesization of arbitrary waveforms
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: In this paper the setting up of a binary Josephson array waveform system for synthesization of arbitrary waveforms is described. The authors are with the Electricity Laboratory in the Metrology and Calibration Centre of INTA (Instituto Nacional de Tecnica Aeroespacial) in Torrejon de Ardoz, Madrid, Spain.

articleTitle: Possible changing in voltage key comparison procedure
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: The progress in developing Josephson voltage system contributes an increasing in the accuracy of the voltage unit transfer. Using the different methods during voltage standard key comparisons allows defining accuracy of compared standard with uncertainty, differing in 10-100 once. Some issues concerning measurement procedure to follow in voltage key comparison are discussed.

articleTitle: The quantum-limited comb lineshape for a mode-locked Ti:Sapphire laser
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: We have calculated the quantum-limited lineshape of the comb lines from a mode-locked Ti:sapphire laser using experimentally-derived parameters for the linear response and quantum noise drivers from a generalized soliton perturbation theory. The detailed lineshape has small contributions from relaxation oscillations and frequency pulling. Our results are relevant in determining the fundamental limitation due to amplified spontaneous emission on the uncertainty of frequency measurements using femtosecond combs.

articleTitle: Bilateral optical fiber power meter linearity comparison between NMIJ and NIST
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Optical fiber power meter (OFPM) linearity standards of NMIJ (Japan) and NIST (USA) are compared using a commercial OFPM as a transfer standard at 1310 nm and 1550 nm over a power range [-60 dBm, 0 dBm]. At both wavelengths the comparison indicates an agreement between the two laboratories within the combined uncertainty. At 1550 nm the uncertainties are larger, which is attributed to unstable operation of the transfer standard at this wavelength.

articleTitle: Nb/Al-AlOx/Nb overdamped junctions suitable for voltage standard operation above 4.2 K
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Nb/Al-AlOx/Nb Josephson junctions of few micrometers size, derived by the basic hysteretic SIS process, have shown stable overdamped current voltage, I-V, characteristic with Ic of 1–10 mA and Vc of 100–600 μV at 4.2 K. The moderate dependence on temperature of these parameters has allowed to use them at temperatures above 4.2 K, near the Nb transition temperature, measuring quantized voltage steps several hundreds μA wide on single and 10 junctions arrays at T ≫ 8 K. This paves the way to their use in cryocooler setup of reduced cost and power consumption for a future generation of programmable and AC voltage standard.

articleTitle: Comparisons of ukrainian national standards of electrical units of the national metrological institute “Ukrmetrteststandard”
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A EUROMET and COOMET key and supplementary comparisons of complex of national standards of electrical units of national metrological institute "Ukrmetrteststandard" in 2000-2007 are considered.

articleTitle: Microwave permittivity and permeability properties and microwave reflections of ferrite powders
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Magnetic powders applications are becoming attractive in electromagnetic shielding interferences in wireless systems. Magnetic powders are also very important in magnetic resonances imaging and as well as the drug delivery applications in biomedical research. As such, a good understanding of the magnetic powders' microwave responses is crucial in modern technological applications. In this paper we present accurate broad-band data on the real and imaginary parts of permeability and permittivity of Ni<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-x-y</sub>Co<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub>Cu<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">y</sub>Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2-z-d</sub>Mn<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">z</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub> and Ni<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-x</sub>Zn<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub>Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2-y</sub>Mn<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">y</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub> substrates in the frequency range of 4 to 40 GHz.

articleTitle: Metrological characterizations of wideband digitizers
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: This paper deals with the characterization of the metrological performance of digitizers so that they can be used for metrology applications. Apart from dc behaviour such as linearity, stability, and noise, especially the dynamic performance of the digitizers is important and thus the measurement of AC flatness, phase, and sample jitter are essential. We present here first results of characterizations of precision sampling voltmeter when DC signals are digitized, with respect of some parameters such as aperture time, "dead" time and autozero.

articleTitle: Precision spectroscopy of atomic hydrogen for an improved Rydberg constant determination
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: The 2S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1/2</sub>-8D<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5/2</sub> transition in atomic hydrogen has been observed as part of the preparation for a Rydberg constant determination at the National Physical Laboratory, UK. We describe this observation and the ongoing improvements to the experimental apparatus.

articleTitle: Measurement of absolute energy level and hyperfine structure of 87Rb 4D5/2 using double resonance optical pumping method
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: We have measured the absolute frequency and the uncertainty of the excited state transition, 5P<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3/2</sub>-4D<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5/2</sub>, in <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">87</sup>Rb atom with a fs frequency comb, utilizing the double resonance optical pumping (DROP) method. The absolute energy level of 4D<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5/2</sub> state is determined by measuring the absolute frequency of the 5S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1/2</sub>-5P<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3/2</sub> transition simultaneously. The hyperfine structure constants of the 4D<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5/2</sub> state are obtained with the magnetic dipole constant uncertainty reduced ten-fold compared to the previous result and with the electric quadrupole constant determined for the first time.

articleTitle: Development of a neutral strontium lattice trap optical clock at the National Physical Laboratory
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: The <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>-<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>P<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> transition in neutral strontium is being considered as one of the choices for the future redefinition of the SI second. At the National Physical Laboratory we are designing and implementing an optical clock based on this transition, holding the atoms in an optical lattice during the clock interrogation cycle, which greatly increases the potential accuracy of the clock. Our focus is on building a compact experimental system (including a novel permanent-magnet-based Zeeman slower) designed with the ability to assess systematic frequency shifts in mind, especially those related to blackbody radiation. Further study of systematic effects and additional intercomparisons of experimental results from different laboratories are being pursued with a view to gaining support for a future redefinition.

articleTitle: The control and measurement of femtosecond laser radiation parameters with Fabry-Perot interferometer
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: The method for measurement of different femtosecond laser radiation parameters using Fabry-Perot interferometer is suggested. The self- mode locked Cr:forsterite laser was used in our experiments. The average wavelength of a laser radiation lambda<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>, laser radiation spectrum width deltalambda and general offset f<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> of frequency comb were determined.

articleTitle: Measurement of above 1 GHz EMC antennas in a fully anechoic room
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: This paper describes a method of measuring the free-space antenna factors of above 1 GHz EMC antennas in a fully anechoic room (FAR) which is validated by comparison with an open area test site (OATS).

articleTitle: Magneto-optical trapping of Yb atoms using an intercombination transition with an optical frequency comb: For realizing an Yb optical lattice clock
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: We have magneto-optically trapped cold ytterbium atoms using an intercombination transition for realizing an optical lattice clock. For this purpose, we have developed a laser-diode-based light source, which is phase-locked to an optical frequency comb, thus attaining both laser frequency stabilization and laser linewidth narrowing.

articleTitle: Development of an ytterbium optical lattice clock at KRISS
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: This paper describes the current status of an ytterbium lattice clock under development at KRISS. After the success of 399 nm magneto-optical-trap (MOT) at a temperature 1 mK, we constructed the 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">nd</sup> stage cooling laser system at a wavelength of 556 nm to cool atoms further down to several muK. We are also developing an ultra-narrow linewidth laser at a wavelength of 578 nm to probe the clock transition by doubling the frequency output of a commercial 1156 nm ECDL. Efforts to reduce the linewidth are under way.

articleTitle: Research of a novel Rogowski coil with special magnetic core
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: This paper presents a novel Rogowski coil with special core. It contains the advantages of both current transformer with iron-core and air coil. It expresses novel characters in principles that the magnetic source is magnetic-particle, it also can be used effectively in high-frequency band. The lineal extent of magnetic intensity is wide and the distortion of transient current will be reduced comparing to transformer with iron-core. The voltage magnitude of Rogowski coil with special magnetic core in open-circuit have been increased greatly comparing to air coil. So RC integrating device can be used to constitute ideal transient current transformer.

articleTitle: Transportability of the NML 1 Ω resistor
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A group of three 1Ω resistors designed and fabricated at the National Measurement Institute, Australia (NMIA), were transported by air freight between NMIA and the U.S. National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) to quantify travel-induced changes in resistance value. The resistors were exchanged between the two laboratories in two successive cycles in 2007–2008. The average travel-induced change was less than 0.02 μΩ/Ω and the maximum change was 0.04 μΩ/Ω. The longterm drift rate of the three resistors, measured over 12 years, was less than 0.01 μΩ/Ω per year.

articleTitle: Magnetic field of the calculable AC/DC resistance standard of toroid type
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: The paper discusses the magnetic field of calculable resistor of toroid type which influences the transform of AC/DC quantum Hall resistances standard. Theoretical models are built based on the complex logarithm transform function. Thus, the distribution of magnetic field can be obtained. It also displays the distribution of main magnetic flux and the leakage flux. Furthermore, the equations of boundary magnetic field line and the position of the boundary on the axis can be calculated theoretically on the model.

articleTitle: Theoretical model of the frequency response coefficient of calculable coaxial resistance standards from DC to 100 MHz
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A theoretical model of the electromagnetic frequency response coefficient (FRC) of high-frequency four terminal-pair calculable coaxial resistance standards (HF-CRS) has been developed. The model includes many factors which are considered to be significant and contribute to the FRC of HF-CRS for frequencies ranging from DC to 100 MHz. Applying the model to practical HF-CRS enables calibration of impedance analysers for resistance over this frequency range.

articleTitle: Validation of inductance measurements at NMi VSL
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: To validate an inductance resonance bridge, which is based on a commercial capacitance bridge, a second resonance bridge was built, based on a self-composed 4 terminal-pair impedance ratio bridge. From analysis of the results on 100 mH standards at 1 kHz, discrepancies have been resolved and the uncertainty has been improved to 26 muH/H.

articleTitle: Sources of normal mode offset in precision DMM’S
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: We investigate the causes of the observed normal mode offsets in precision DMM’s. With a circuit simulation tool to model the front-end amplifier we have been able to qualitatively reproduce the observed offset in a commonly used 8.5 digit precision DMM. In general the cause of the offset is related to the symmetry of the front-end architecture. However it seems there are several mechanisms which contribute to the effect, and it is these that we are presently seeking to elucidate.

articleTitle: 556 NM light generation by frequency doubling of a diode laser amplifed Yb-doped fiber amplifer for precision spectroscopy of ytterbium atoms
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: We have developed a simple laser system for generation of coherent 556 nm light by using frequency doubling of a diode laser. 1112 nm light from an external cavity diode laser is amplified via Yb-doped fiber amplifier and 200 mW of the amplified light is injected to wave-guided MgO-doped PPLN, which produces a 30 mW green light. The frequency diode laser is stabilized to a resonance peak of a high-finesse cavity with finesse ~10000.

articleTitle: Stabilization study of resistive thin films for ac resistors application
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: This paper presents results on the development of metallic ultra thin films on cylindrical alumina substrate, which are the basis of coaxial ac resistors. Ni<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">80</sub>Cr<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">20</sub> and Ni<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">75</sub>Cr<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">20</sub>Al<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2.5</sub>Cu<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2.5</sub> materials alloy have been used for synthesizing the resistive layers by magnetron sputtering technique. Resistance values as high as 100 k Omega and 200 k Omega have been obtained for both materials respectively over the short substrate length of 45 mm. The characteristics of the layers as homogeneity, thickness, resistances values and stability have been determined and discussed according to the deposit conditions. Specific heat treatments are developed to improve load-life stability of the films.

articleTitle: High confined Bragg modes for very low phase noise oscillator and narrow band filtering applications
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: This paper describes the use of a new resonator using a hybrid Bragg mode (HBM) with azimuthal variations greater than zero. Usually Bragg modes require a pure Transverse Electric mode with no azimuthal variations and only electric field component, E<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">θ</inf> The mode is both Bragg-like, (E<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf> is tangential to all dielectric boundaries) and also whispering gallery-like, (possesses azimuthal variations). This new dielectric resonator has superior performance with respect to typical dielectric resonators at room temperature. A resonance was observed at 13.4 GHz with an unloaded Q-factor of order 2×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sup> in an Alumina structure, which is more than a factor of six above the dielectric loss limit.

articleTitle: Comparison of fundamental-constant based definitions for the kilogram and the ampere
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: We have determined the influence of alternative definitions for the kilogram and the ampere on the uncertainty of h, e and m<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">u</sub>. This has been achieved with a least-squares adjustment of a limited set of observational equations. We have evaluated the residual errors (and their uncertainties) from this adjustment, and used these to determine expansion factors to achieve results that are self-consistent. This enables us, inter alia, to evaluate the extent to which the experimentally-determined values of the "electrical" constants are sufficiently self-consistent to be used as the motivation for any proposed redefinition.

articleTitle: Improved Cryogenic Current Comparator setup with digital double current source
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Resistance calibration at PTB, Germany’s national metrological institute (NMI), has been based on Cryogenic Current Comparators (CCC’s) for almost two decades [1]. So far, comparisons in the ensemble of normal resistors with nominal values from 1 Ω up to 1 MΩ and with the quantum Hall resistance R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">K-90</inf> are performed by means of two complementary setups for high- or low-ohmic resistors, respectively. To replace both setups, we designed a new LHe probe equipped with an optimized PTB dc SQUID sensor as well as a digital state-of-the-art double-current source. In this paper, we describe basic features and highlight the advantages of the new system.

articleTitle: Optical frequency measurement using an optical frequency comb generator based on frequency shifted feedback fiber ring laser
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: We present an optical frequency comb generator (OFCG) based on a fiber ring laser that provides a bandwidth of over 700 GHz with modeless operation. The OFCG was developed via a configuration with frequency shifted feedback fiber ring laser utilizing an acousto-optic modulator (AOM) with a carrier frequency of 150 MHz when acetylene stabilized laser was injected into the fiber ring cavity as a seeding laser. The comb frequency stability of OFCG was estimated to be 3.3 times 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-10</sup> for a Is averaging time. The OFCG was used to evaluate the frequency measurement of test laser (unstabilized laser).

articleTitle: Impruving of the relative conductivity measurements traceability to primary standards of resistance, length and temperature
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Dependence of the relative conductivity measurements on resistance standard, length standard and temperature standard is analyzed. Results of conductivity measurement traceability improving are given. Appropriate constructions of the cell and resistive measuring systems are discussed.

articleTitle: More than 200 mW blue light source from an integrative ring cavity
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: An integrative external-enhancement ring cavity has been designed to acquire 461 nm blue light source with high output power. Using a 30-mm-long quasi-phase-matched periodically-poled KTP doubling crystal, we have obtained total more than 210 mW blue light from 287 mW coupling incident power with the net conversion efficiency over 70%.

articleTitle: A new method to measure the dielectric loss of Teflon specimen in cylindrical tube shape
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: The Teflon frame is used in establishing NIM’s AC Resistance Calculable Standard. Comparison with the suspended design such as coaxial, quadrifilar and octofilar types, the frame of resistor gives better stability. However, the dielectric loss of Teflon frame will bring additional ac/dc difference. To measure this dielectric loss precisely, a new measurement structure is provided and the substitute method is carried out to decrease the uncertainty from instrument. The measurement uncertainty of dissipation factor is estimated as several parts in 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sup>.

articleTitle: AC power standard at frequencies up to 200 kHz
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: The paper describes a standard system for traceable measurements of electrical power of sinusoidal signals at voltages up to 1000 V, currents up to 20 A and frequencies from 40 Hz to 200 kHz. The system uses thermoelectric effects to relate the alternating power to that of known dc signals. It is comprised of a thermal power comparator, inductive and resistive voltage dividers and a range of wideband current shunts. The performance of each of the components has been evaluated through traceable measurements, in terms of fundamental standards. The standard uncertainties range from less than 5 muW/VA at power frequencies to 60 muW/VA - 250 muW/VA at 200 kHz.

articleTitle: Experimental realisation of the quantum metrological triangle experiment at LNE: Set-up and first results
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: We describe the experimental set-up used at LNE for closing the quantum metrological triangle (QMT) experiment and also testing the quantization of a current generated by a single electron device. Our present device is an R-electron pump composed of 3 tunnel junctions. The influence of the pumping frequency on the noise and on the current stability is firstly investigated. Then preliminary results are given about the quantized current measured with the complete QMT set-up. A relative random uncertainty of a few parts in 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sup> has been found for a 100 MHz pumping frequency.

articleTitle: High resolution spectroscopy using fiber laser frequency combs
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: The output of a femtosecond fiber laser can be both spectrally broadened and stabilized, thereby providing a broadband coherent source in the near infrared. In the frequency domain, the result is a frequency comb with frequency stabilities at the millihertz level (relative to the reference), while in the time domain, the result is an optical pulse train with sub-femtosecond relative timing jitter. This coherent source can be used for high-resolution measurements in a range of areas including frequency metrology, ranging, vibrometry, and spectroscopy. We will discuss the performance of these sources, focusing on recent work applying them to high-resolution spectroscopy. This contribution of NIST, an agency of the US government, is not subject to copyright.

articleTitle: Silicon lattice-parameter measurements with centimeter x-ray interferometry
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A combined x-ray and optical interferometer capable of centimeter displacements has been realized to measure the lattice parameter of a <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">28</sup>Si crystal to within a 3 x 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-9</sup> relative uncertainty. This paper relates the results of test measurements carried out to assess the capabilities of the new apparatus.

articleTitle: First-order sideband pulling in atomic frequency standards
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: High performance frequency standards, including cesium fountains and most optical standards, operate with pulsed measurements repeated at a fixed frequency. By introducing frequency modulation of the excitation coherent with the measurement cycle time, we have observed biases in the primary frequency standard NIST-F1 much larger than biases predicted by previous theories. We derive a theory of such biases for both Rabi and Ramsey excitation. We find agreement with the experimental measurements.

articleTitle: Quantum hall effect in graphene
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Graphene is the first example of truly two-dimensional crystals - it's just one layer of carbon atoms. It turns out that graphene is a gapless semiconductor with unique electronic properties resulting from the fact that charge carriers in graphene obey linear dispersion relation, thus mimicking massless relativistic particles. This results in the observation of a number of very peculiar electronic properties - from an anomalous quantum Hall effect (QHE) to the absence of localization. It also provides a bridge between condensed matter physics and quantum electrodynamics and opens new perspectives for carbon-based electronics.

articleTitle: Magneto-resistance oscillations and zero-resistance states induced by photo-excitation in the quasi two-dimensional GaAs/AlGaAs system
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Photo-excitation of high quality two dimensional electron systems induces "1/4 cycle shifted" inverse- B-periodic magnetoresistance oscillations with nodes in the resistance at B<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">f</sub> / j for the fundamental series, where j is a positive integer or half integer, B<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">f</sub> is the characteristic magnetic field that increases with the radiation frequency, f, as B<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">f</sub> = 2pi f m*/e, m* is an electron effective mass, and e is the electron charge. At the lowest temperatures and modest magnetic fields, vanishing diagonal resistance is observed at the resistance minima as in the quantum Hall situation, without concomitant plateaus in the Hall effect. Here, we describe and review the remarkable features of these novel effects.

articleTitle: Uniformity of electron pumping regime in two GaAs tunable-barrier pumps
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: We show that quantised tunable-barrier electron pumping can be implemented in two different samples of GaAs device using the same control parameters. This is an important step towards the realization of a parallel pump architecture for generating quantised currents of up to 10 nA.

articleTitle: The SI between evolution and revolution
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Some critical points of the planned redefinitions of SI units are considered in view of the overall consistency of the system and of its evolution from standard-based to constant-based definitions. Also the relevance of a most radical proposal, among those already advanced, is stressed and some consequences are identified.

articleTitle: Performances and progress of a compact pulsed CPT Cs clock
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: We report on the development of a compact Cs cell CPT frequency standard operating in the Dicke regime. Combining a double Lambda scheme and a Ramsey interrogation, high contrast fringes whose linewidth depends on the time separating two pulses, are obtained. Compared to the continuous regime, the pulsed interrogation reduces the light shift by a factor 300 and permits to reach frequency stability 10 times better. A frequency stability of 9.10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−13</sup> at 1 s has already been measured.

articleTitle: Novel transfer standard for temperature measurements of The International Avogadro project
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: The International Avogadro Coordination aims at determining the Avogadro constant by measuring the molar mass, lattice parameter and density of a <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">28</sup>Si single crystal. As the temperature dependent quantities are measured in different apparatuses, the consistency of the temperature measurements has to be proven. An electronic temperature reference and a standard platinum resistance thermometer (SPRT) are used - in a first round - to compare the temperature measurements at the INRIM and PTB.

articleTitle: Compendium for precise ac measurements of the quantized Hall resistance
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: At its 2006 meeting, the Working Group of the Comite Consultatif d'Electricite et Magnetisme (CCEM) on the AC quantum Hall effect requested that the authors write a compendium which integrates the experiences of a collaboration between NRC, METAS, and PTB focusing on AC measurements of the quantized Hall resistance (ac QHR). This compendium summarizes the present state of the authors' knowledge and reviews the experiences, tests and precautions to achieve accurate measurements of the AC quantum Hall effect. This work shows that the ac quantum Hall effect can be reliably used as a quantum standard of AC resistance having a relative uncertainty of a few parts in 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">8</sup>.

articleTitle: Rabi microwave power standard
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: The performance of a quantum based microwave power standard is presented. The measured incident power is compared to a known value. In order to improve the comparison we have developed, a waveguide micro calorimeter. We have also rebuilt part of the instrument. Results from both systems will be presented.

articleTitle: Stepping up AC-DC current up to 20 A
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: This paper describes the AC/DC current stepping up arrangement and results at the National Metrology Centre (NMC). Planar multi-junction thermal converters (PMJTCs) were used with a set of coaxial current shunts to build up the AC-DC current transfer standards for the range from 10 mA to 20 A at frequency range of 10 Hz to 100 kHz. Current level-dependence of the PMJTCs at low frequencies was determined experimentally. The resulted AC-DC differences agree well with known calibration with expanded uncertainties of less than 55 muA/A at 20 A for frequencies from 10 Hz to 100 kHz.

articleTitle: Progress on the GAMS-6 double crystal γ-spectrometer
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Measuring the wavelength of gamma-rays emitted after a neutron capture reaction allows a direct determination of the molar Planck constant N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">A</inf>h. Currently these measurements are realized using the high resolution double crystal spectrometers GAMS4 and GAMS5 placed at the high flux reactor of the Institut Laue-Langevin in Grenoble, France. So far it was possible to achieve a relative uncertainty of 4×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−7</sup>. In this contribution we describe the progress in building a new generation crystal spectrometer, GAMS 6, which is meant to lower the uncertainty to the 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−8</sup> level.

articleTitle: Realization of a robust single-parameter quantized charge pump
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: This paper describes a novel scheme for quantized charge pumping based on single-parameter modulation. The device is realized in an AlGaAs-GaAs gated nanowire. A particular advantage of this realization is that operation in the quantized regime can be achieved in a potentially large range of amplitude and dc off-set of the driving signal. This feature together with the simple configuration might enable large scale parallel operation of many such devices.

articleTitle: Zero collisional frequency shift operation of a caesium fountain clock
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: We report preliminary results from a Cs fountain primary frequency standard operated in a regime where the collisional frequency shift is zero. This shift is of opposite sign for the two clock states. The shift is cancelled by equalizing the contributions from the two clock states by adjusting the clock state composition during the microwave interrogation. Design details of, and modifications to, the fountain NPL-CsF2 are described. Attention has been paid to assuring long-term stability of the fountain parameters, especially the atom cloud size and the amplitude of the interrogating microwave field.

articleTitle: A new test method for electrical conductivity of aviation fuel
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A new coaxial cylindrical cell with guard electrodes has constructed and a unique approach to determine the cell constant by means of capacitance of the cell in air has been presented. The new cell is very stable in both construction and performance. With this technique, an uncertainty of 0.1% in measuring conductivity of aviation fuel and other liquids can be achieved.

articleTitle: Measurement of the gravitational constant with a mass comparator
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: We have measured Newton's gravitational constant with a commercially available mass comparator. In this experiment, the difference of the gravitational force of 13,600 kg mercury on two 1.1 kg copper masses was measured with a relative statistical uncertainty of 16.3times10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-6</sup>. Including the systematic uncertainties we determine the gravitational constant G to be 6.674 252(122)times10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-11</sup> m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>kg<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>s<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-2</sup>.

articleTitle: Study on the problem of channel-closing of multi-channel comparator for heavy direct current
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: To solve the problem of channel-closing of multichannel comparator for heavy direct current, a new method is proposed that an air gap is set between every two channels in the DC comparator. This method fairly prevents the channels of multi-channel comparator from closing, and guarantees high precision measurement. By calculation, the comparator of four channels, with the total length of air gaps to be 3.2 mm and the length of each gap to be 0.8 mm, has the current ratio accuracy higher than 5 times 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-4</sup> when applied for industrial measurement.

articleTitle: High-precision linearity standard for high-power optical-fiber power meters
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A high-precision linearity standard for high-power optical fiber power meters (OFPMs) at 1550 nm is developed using an integrating sphere and an InGaAs photodiode connected to a picoammeter. Its linearity is evaluated in the superposition method, where optical signals are superposed in the integrating sphere using a two-core ferrule to avoid high loss and high-power instability of an otherwise used fiber coupler. The uncertainty (k=1) of this standard's linearity at 1 W with reference power 1 mW is less than 0.002 dB. Test OFPMs' linearity is calibrated by comparison with this standard within an extended uncertainty (k=2) of 0.005 dB at 1 W.

articleTitle: Bi-lateral comparison of V-band antenna gain between KRISS and NIST
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A bi-lateral comparison of power gain for a V-band (50 GHz - 75 GHz) Cassegrain antenna and a standard horn antenna has been performed between KRISS and NIST. This paper describes the comparison and its progress so far. Measurement results will be presented at the conference.

articleTitle: NIST reference spectral responsivity scales for improving the SI candela and kelvin
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Both SI units, the candela and the kelvin were originally derived from standard blackbody sources. Recently, instead of source-based calibrations, they both have been realized with optical detector standards. Recent decrease of the measurement uncertainties in detector-based calibrations resulted in improved uncertainties in these SI units.

articleTitle: Systematic error analysis of stepwise approximated AC waveforms generated by a Programmable Josephson Voltage Standard
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: We have measured stepwise-approximated sinewaves generated by a programmable Josephson voltage standard with several different output configurations. These data are analyzed to characterize the dominant error mechanisms for rms applications, such as ac-dc difference measurements of a thermal voltage converter (TVC). We discuss the impact of the dominant systematic errors on the overall uncertainty and consider the implications of providing the load current required by low input impedance devices such as TVC's.

articleTitle: Measuring flicker with discrete fourier transform
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: This paper describes a new standard for precision measurements of flicker. Two different methods are used and compared. The absolute standard uncertainty (1sigma) is estimated to be a few parts in 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sup>.

articleTitle: A thin-film AC-DC thermal converter with V02 resistive sensing
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: We propose a thin-film thermal converter with resistive sensing of the temperature rise of the heater. Vanadium oxide (V0<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) is used for the sensing resistors. This paper shows the simulations used for the basic design. The high temperature coefficient of its resistivity and the optimization of the design envisage a sensitivity of 10 V·W<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup>

articleTitle: The BIPM G experiment — Final results
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: This paper gives the final results of the Mk II version of the BIPM torsion-balance G experiment. Results of the Mk I version were published in 2001 and the apparatus was entirely rebuilt in the years 2001 to 2003. The key feature the BIPM approach is that a value of G can be obtained by up to three different methods. The 2001 result came from two methods, which agreed with each other closely. The present work is producing results from three different methods and the considerable challenge to be described in this paper is to obtain agreement among the three.

articleTitle: A compact high-precision voltage standard based on programmable Josephson array
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: This paper describes a compact, portable, high-precision voltage standard based on 1 V programmable Josephson array. The accuracy of the system is estimated to be better than 4 nV. The system can realize the fully automatic measurement of voltage reference, as well as its weight and volume are reduced. "In August, 2007 this system was carried to PTB, Germany to make a comparison. The difference is about 1 nV.

articleTitle: Femtosecond optical frequency comb laser based on cesium 6s–8s 822 nm hyperfine transition
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: We construct a highly stable comb laser based on one compact 822 nm diode laser and one 25-mm long cesium vapor cell, for the first time to our knowledge. It is advantaged that more than 99% comb laser power could be delivered to user since no any nonlinear process is needed for locking laser frequency. The relative merits of atomic transition- based frequency combs are discussed and we demonstrated a novel way on controlling and scanning the carrier-envelop offset frequency by shifting slightly the pump beam.

articleTitle: Status of the international effort on the x-ray crystal density work and its progress towards a measurement of the Avogadro constant
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: The present status of an international attempt of several national metrology institutes to determine the Avogadro constant with a relative standard uncertainty better than 2ldr10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-8</sup> is presented. To this end, a world-wide collaboration has been set up to produce a 5 kg <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">28</sup>Si single crystal with an enrichment factor greater than 99.985%. Technological steps for the growth of the <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">28</sup>Si single crystal, manufacturing of two 1 kg <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">28</sup>Si spheres, and first experimental results are reported.

articleTitle: Feasibility of a Wideband Calculable Standard Antenna for EMC Measurements
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A wideband bi-conical antenna is presented which its input impedance (without Balun) is matched to 50 Omega for 100 MHz to 2 GHz. By its constant gain and slight variation of radiation pattern for this frequency range, the antenna can be used as low-uncertainty calculable standard of e-field. Preliminary results are reported.

articleTitle: Improving the accuracy of the on-site calibrations of multi-function electrical standards
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: This paper describes some improvements to the accuracy of the on-site measuring system of the National Research Council of Canada (NRC) Travelling Standard Program. This NRC service provides traceable calibrations of the multifunction electrical standards that electrical utilities and other organizations use to test and verify electricity revenue meters. The calibration program can be used to show that the measurements of the electricity revenue meters are traceable to the national standard, a requirement of the trade metrology legislation in Canada.

articleTitle: Semi automated dc-squid based CCC bridge for precision resistance measurements at the Spanish TPYCEA
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A semi automated Cryogenic Current Comparator (CCC) system for precision resistance measurements, R<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">X</sub>(Omega), has been developed within a joint collaboration ICMA-TPYCEA. The system, installed at TPYCEA, has an uncertainty of plusmn8ldr10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-9ldr</sup>R<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">X</sub> (k=1) and is being used in conjunction with the previously developed Quantum Hall Resistance system.

articleTitle: Estimating uncertainty limits in the NIST-2008 electronic kilogram
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
