abstract: The NIST electronic kilogram has had three published results with successively smaller uncertainties. In the present design, there are several measurement components that have uncertainties that are difficult to reduce further. These limiting uncertainties are discussed.

articleTitle: Direct stabilization of femtosecond laser frequency comb to high-finesse optical cavity
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: We report a stabilization of a femtosecond laser frequency comb (FLFC) to a high-finesse optical cavity by introducing a comb injection locked diode laser. In our method, single component of a FLFC is selected and amplified by a diode laser, and used for a stabilization of a FLFC. Thus, we don't need to match the mode spacing between a femtosecond laser and a high-finesse optical cavity.

articleTitle: A magnetic levitation technique for the simultaneous comparison of mass artifacts in air and vacuum
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: We describe a mass comparison system in which a test mass artifact in air can be directly compared to a standard mass artifact in vacuum using the same high precision comparator balance. The system uses a magnetic levitation technique to couple the weighing pan of the comparator balance in vacuum to the test mass in air. We will discuss motivation, design considerations, and preliminary results.

articleTitle: Latest Measurements with the LNE-SYRTE Fountain Clocks
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: This paper reports our works on the 3 LNE-SYRTE fountains and their frequency comparisons. We have performed new experiments on the frequency shifts related to the microwave synthesis and to the blackbody radiation interaction. We have also refined the accuracy budget of the <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">87</sup>Rb hyperfine splitting and obtained a new measurement of the frequency comparison between Cesium and Rubidium.

articleTitle: Precise calibration on DC voltage
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: DC voltage was traced to DC voltage reference (FLUKE 732A) by the calibrated divider (datron 4902S). The divider supplied 18 fixed ratios to calibrate DC voltage from 10 mV to 1000 V. DC voltage traceability mainly depends on the DC voltage reference and DC voltage divider. The DCV reference is traced to JJAVS twice a year, with the uncertainty of 1 times 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-7</sup> (k=l). After calibration, the uncertainty of DCV ratios can reach 1 times 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-7</sup>(k=l). As for daily calibration, the uncertainty of DC voltage depends on the long term stability of DCV ratios and the voltage effect of the ratios.

articleTitle: Magnetic permeability, losses and ferromagnetic resonance in ferrites under magnetic field bias from DC to the microwave regime
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Fluxmetric and transmission line methods have been combined to achieve accurate determination of energy loss and complex permeability in soft ferrites from DC to microwave frequencies. Superposition of the results in the MHz frequency range proves instrumental to obtain reproducible data and traceability to the appropriate standards. Permeability curves are strongly affected by ferromagnetic resonance, which can be frequency shifted using a bias field applied transverse to the AC exciting field. The permeability behavior can be correctly predicted by physical modeling, allowing one to separate domain wall and rotational processes, respectively associated with pure relaxation effects and bias field dependent damped resonant behavior.

articleTitle: An accurate asynchronous calculation method for evaluating peak and RMS values from sampled data
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: In high voltage testing there is a need to measure both the peak value and rms value of power frequency voltage. This paper describes method to calculate accurately both quantities; even when the frequency is not stable. The method can handle waveforms with harmonic content, and an uncertainty of few ppm can be achieved. Method is not sensitive to frequency fluctuation and phase lock loop is not needed.

articleTitle: Reproducibility of the quantum hall effect in GaAs/AlGaAs two dimensional electron gas
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: This paper describes an experiment which shows that the integer quantum Hall effect implemented in GaAs/AIGaAs Hall bars mounted as a Wheatstone bridge is reproducible with a relative uncertainty of less than 4 parts in 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sup>.

articleTitle: Density measurement of a small 28Si single crystal
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: The density of an isotopically enriched <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">28</sup>Si crystal is evaluated. A transfer standard of the hollow silicon cylinder is prepared and its density is determined by the hydrostatic weighing (HW). The <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">28</sup>Si crystal is then compared with the hollow silicon for the determination of the density by the pressure-of-flotation (PF) measurement.

articleTitle: A consideration for electrical nonlinear distortion voltage caused by 2D type bridge with very low frequency current
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: It must need to take off the cause of nonlinearity if someone needs a good resistor. The 3<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">rd</sup> harmonic distortion voltages of three types of resistors were measured. In the next stage, the 3<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">rd</sup> harmonic voltage is tested using by a bridge made on a printed circuit board (PCB) occurs current constriction effectively. It is very simple structure without contact barriers to consider the cause of nonlinear distortion. It is obvious that the short bridge causes the high distortion voltage. It seems that heat oscillation for power dissipation and propagation of one cycle of AC current from both bride edges to wide areas of PCB would cause the 3<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">rd</sup> harmonic distortion voltage. In this study, further testing with very low frequency current is superposed to check the AC heating effect is prevented by the low frequency current.

articleTitle: Extended precision measurements of a strontium single ion optical frequency standard and its development as an optical atomic clock
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: We describe the recent advances of the NRC single ion based optical frequency standard using the 445-THz S-D transition in <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">88</sup>Sr<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup>. Laser cooled confinement and probing of the clock transition has been obtained for periods exceeding 24 hours showing high levels of stability. Spectral resolutions better than 5 Hz at 445 THz have been obtained. Work is described on the development of an improved ion trap system and the continuous linkage of the optical frequency to the RF domain using a fiber based frequency comb.

articleTitle: Metrological researces of proton and optical pumping geomagnetometers
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: The results of calibration of proton, cesium, potassium and helium-cesium scalar magnetometers in the range 20-100 muT are discussed. The calibration made it possible to apply corrections to reduce the uncertainty of measurements. Experimental data were obtained using a standard calibration system designed in the D.I. Mendeleyev Metrology Institute (VNIIM).

articleTitle: Monitoring system of isolation transformer power supply
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: This paper reports a new design of power monitor system, which is mainly used in the area of isolation transformer power supply for precision measurement, medical equipments and electrical safety. The principle, structure and function of the system are described in detail.

articleTitle: Design and characterization of a low voltage divider
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: This paper describes the design and characterization of a low voltage divider with 100:1, 1000:1 and 10000:1 ratios in which, if the divider is supplied with 10 V will provide 100 mV, 10 mV and 1 mV outputs of high stability, low noise, low output impedance and stable thermal EMFs whose effects can be further reduced.

articleTitle: Permeability and permittivity measurements using propagation and impedance of TRL calibrated microstriplines
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Numerous wireless communication devices such as integrated circuits and micro biochips are emerging in the 1 to 4 GHz frequency range. Thus it has become crucial to accurately determine the permeability and permittivity of such materials and devices in this spectral range. In this paper, we present a propagation and impedance technique for the microstripline. Three different substrates (Alumina, Silicon dioxide and Beryllium Oxide) are employed to design TRL sets for measurement purposes. The custom-designed TRL sets return losses of up to -50 dB which is the same as a standard waveguide TRL calibration.

articleTitle: Low voltage AC-DC transfer standards at LNE
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: This paper describes the method used to establish the traceability of LNE AC-DC transfer standards in the mV-range to the 1 V multijunction converter, which serves as the primary AC-DC standard. Main uncertainty components are listed and final uncertainty given for the different voltage levels. An independent method was developed for the calibration of thermal converters at 0.3 V and 0.2 V. The agreement between this method and the step-down is within the standard uncertainty.

articleTitle: First experiment of precise time transfer using ETS-VIII satellite
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: The Engineering Test Satellite-VIII (ETS-VIII) is a Japanese geostationary satellite. Its missions include basic satellite positioning experiments using on-board atomic clocks. The NICT (National Institute of Information and Communications Technology) developed special equipment for this time transfer link. This link makes precise time transfer between the on-board atomic clock and a ground reference clock using two-way time transfer method and carrier phase measurement for the first time in the world. We expect to obtain an exceedingly precision as few ps between both clocks. We also estimated the range between the satellite and the ground station using the time transfer data.

articleTitle: Remote frequency control via IEEE 1588
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A new scheme of remote frequency control based on the IEEE 1588 standards, a precision time synchronization protocol (PTP) is proposed in this paper. A remote oven-controlled crystal oscillator (OCXO) is steered by integrating the PTP system, fuzzy controller and D/A converter, such that its frequency can follow a primary cesium atomic clock used as the master clock of the PTP system. Experimental results show that for averaging times of one day, the frequency stability of the OCXO can be improved from a few parts in 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">9</sup> to 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</sup>.

articleTitle: Development of a calculable potential transformer with a wide ratio error of −10 % to +10 % and its application
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A calculable potential transformer (PT) with a nominal ratio error of -10 % to +10 % has been developed on basis of theoretical calculation of ratio error by the number of primary windings. The developed wide ratio error PT (WRE PT) can be used to evaluate the linearity and accuracy of the PT comparator by comparing both the theoretical and experimental values of the WRE PT. The WRE PT has been applied for the on-site calibration and correction of the PT comparator up to wide ratio error range of -10%to+10%.

articleTitle: Precision high resolution fourier transform spectroscopy of greenhouse gases at millimeter and submillimeter wavelengths
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Dispersive Fourier transform spectroscopy (DFTS) provides us with a very effective technique for the measurement of absorption and refractive index spectra of environmentally hazardous gases. This paper presents the rotational transition lines and refractive index spectra of Nitrous Oxide gas as a function of varying pressure using DFTS for the very first time. The relationship between the variation of the pressure and the change in the absorption spectrum is examined and discussed in detail. Nitrous Oxide (NO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>) gas is considered a harmful greenhouse gas and is the third largest contributor to overall global warming after Carbon Dioxide and Methane. This study demonstrates the ability of our setup to accurately identify and characterize NO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> gas at differing pressures over a broadband frequency spectrum. These findings presented from 300 GHz - 900 GHz are therefore of great importance in the ongoing struggle to battle global warming.

articleTitle: Studies on AC voltage measurement by sampling method
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Digital sampling measuring system was developed at NIM. AC signals under test were transmitted into the input of AD converter by voltage follower. Under the control of MCU□AD converter synchronously sampled the signal by full period, and the sampling data was transmitted by photo-coupler and calculated by computer. The sampling results compared with the measurement results of FLUKE 5790A. The agreements were within 2×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−5</sup>. It was found that the dominating part of the uncertainty in the system is the Integral Nonlinearity (INL) of AD converter, and the influence of quantization error can be decreased by increasing the sampling frequency.

articleTitle: Determination of the fine structure constant with atom interferometry and Bloch oscillations on 87Rb atoms
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: We report a new measurement of the atomic recoil using atom interferometry and Bloch oscillations in a vertical accelerated optical lattice. For the first time, we combine the high efficiency of Bloch oscillations with the sensitivity of Ramsey-Borde interferometer. The new determination of the fine structure constant alpha is in very good agreement with our previous non interferometric one. The uncertainties of our values of alpha are smaller than the uncertainty of any other value except those deduced from the measurements of the electron magnetic moment anomaly a<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">e</sub>.

articleTitle: Single-frequency synthesis at telecommunication wavelengths
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: We have developed an optical single-frequency synthesizer for telecommunications wavelengths. The synthesizer is based on a conventional Ti:S frequency comb generator and generates a single user-specified frequency within the 192-196 THz gain bandwidth of the erbium-doped fiber amplifier from an atomic time base. The synthesized frequency can be directly used, e.g., for spectroscopy, high precision characterization of optical components, or as a reference in calibration of acetylene-stabilized lasers.

articleTitle: Determination of the farad from dc quantum hall effect, by using digital ac bridges
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A new traceability chain for the derivation of the farad from dc quantum Hall effect is under characterization at INRIM. Main steps are performed by new ratio and quadrature coaxial ac bridges. The bridges are based on a polyphase digital synthesizer and do not employ variable dividers or impedances to achieve equilibrium. Preliminary measurements show an agreement, between the new farad determination and the maintained unit, better than 2 times 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-7</sup>.

articleTitle: Development of a calibration system of digital recorders for impulse tests
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: The configuration of a calibration system of digital recorder(digitizer) for HV impulse measurement is described. The system is developed based on Labview. Its calibration methods are according to IEC61083-1-2001, excepted for a fitting algorithm introduced in the determination of static non-linearity for digital recorder. The calibration system has been applied to the calibration of 8-bit and 300MHz digital recorder.

articleTitle: Pulsed optically pumped rubidium atomic clock with optical detection
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: We describe the ongoing work on a <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">87</sup>Rb vapor-cell atomic clock using pulsed optical pumping with an optical detection technique. In order to eliminate the light shifts and to increase the stability of vapor-cell atomic clock, pulsed optical pumping technique has been used. For simplicity, direct laser absorption signal is used for the detection of a clock transition.

articleTitle: CCEM comparison CCEM.RF-K19. CL: attenuation at 60 MHz and 5 GHz using a type N step attenuator
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: This paper presents the results of an international comparison for the measurement of RF attenuation at 60 MHz and 5 GHz. Twenty National Metrology Institutes were involved in this comparison, which took place between January 2002 and January 2007. On the whole, the results show a good agreement amongst the participants.

articleTitle: Precise measuring system for traceability of high current transformer standards
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Results of development of precise low frequency measuring system for traceability of high current transformer standards are given. Comparative investigations of developed standards on Russian Federation primary standard where been provided and results are shown.

articleTitle: A new method on measuring the level dependence of AC shunts
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: We describe a method of the measurement of level dependence in AC-DC difference of current shunts. The method is based on the use of a binary inductive bridge. The measuring principle and measurement results of a 1 A AC shunt at frequencies up to 100 kHz are presented.

articleTitle: The 2006 adjustment of the fundamental constants: Looking towards 2010
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A new set of values of the basic fundamental constants has been recommended by the Committee on Data for Science and Technology (CODATA) (http://phvsics.nist.gov/cuu/Constants/). It is based on a least-squares adjustment that incorporates new data that became available before the closing date of 31 December 2006 (known as the 2006 LSA). A number of key advances in experiment and theory have led to significant improvements in our knowledge of the values of the constants. The consequences of the new results and how the values were determined will be discussed.

articleTitle: Research of transfer quantum hall resistance with direct current comparator bridge instrument
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: The problems of transfer Quantum Hall resistance to 1 Ω resistance standard with direct current comparator bridge (DCC) are introduced. Some effective technique ways are suggested by analyzing the possible causations of the measurement results’ fluctuation. The comparing experiments between DCC and cryogenic current comparator bridge (CCC) have been performed with analyzing the uncertainty of measurement results. The transfer uncertainty from Quantum Hall resistance to 1 Ω standard with DCC is 3×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−8</sup> (k=1), which is enough accurate in practical resistance standard calibration of metrology.

articleTitle: Sampling precision consideration for high resolution Fourier transform spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: The use of dispersive Fourier transform techniques in interferometry allows the measurement of absorption coefficient and refractive index spectra with great precision. Normally, the sharp rotational lines of gaseous molecules can be resolved once higher resolution spectroscopy is employed. The high resolution requires recording of interferogram data points over an extended mirror movement. The issue of sampling size was never considered in the past. This paper presents the importance of using precise step motors for data sampling in these highly sensitive measurements by using two different step motors.

articleTitle: Precision haddad-type calculable resistors
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Coaxial resistors with a calculable frequency dependence have been realized at PTB as a part of the chain from the DC quantized Hall resistance to the capacitance standard. The construction of resistors with nominal value of 1000 Omega and 1290.64 Omega is described. A modified construction of the original Haddad resistor allows a full dismantling while the outer shielding is intact, and the resistance is adjustable within 10-10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-6</sup>.

articleTitle: About the IEEE instrumentation and measurement society
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Presents information about the IEEE Instrumentation and Measurement Society.

articleTitle: CPEM 2008 Technical Sessions
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Provides a schedule of conference events and a listing of which papers were presented in each session.

articleTitle: 2008 conference on precision electromagnetic digest [Front Matter and Copyright]
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: The following topics are dealt with: fundamental constant, resistance, ac-dc transfer, voltage, power, impedance, magnetic variable, time and frequency measurements and standards; calibration of measurement techniques and set-ups; photonic and magnetic methods; radiofrequency measurement methods.

articleTitle: Author index
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: The author index contains an entry for each author and coauthor included in the proceedings record.

articleTitle: Research on SVM-based large signal behavior model method for RF power amplifier
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A single S parameter is sufficient for small signal networks analysis, but more mathematical tools are needed to describe and interpret the data resulted from large signal networks analysis. In this article, a SVM-based approach is adopted to describe nonlinear characteristic of RF power components: nonlinear scattering function. The nonlinear scattering function can build accurate behavior model of RF power components under large signal.

articleTitle: NiCr based thin film cryo resistors
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Thin film resistors, based on the NiCr alloys, have been fabricated and studied at temperatures down to 50 mK. Resistivity of the films varied within (7-11) Ohm*square depending on additions of Cu, Al and Ge. The resistors demonstrate Kondo minimum at 20 K - 30 K. Power dependence measurements at sub Kelvin temperatures showed an electron overheating at the power level above 10 pW for the Ni<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">75</sub>Cr<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">20</sub>Cu<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2.5</sub>Al<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2.5</sub> (Evanohm) 500 kOhm film resistor.

articleTitle: Reference method for small circular loop antennas in the MF and HF bands
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Generally, the standard field method is widely employed in the loop antenna calibration at many national metrology institutes and calibration service laboratories. On the other hand, a calibration method is necessary to be traceable to the standard of magnetic antenna factor. In this study, we propose a reference antenna method for circular loop antennas in the low-frequency bands.

articleTitle: Intrinsically stable CCC for accurate measurement of small currents
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: We have developed and tested an intrinsically stable cryogenic current comparator (CCC) with a 1:20000 winding ratio for the accurate measurement of small electrical currents. Key feature of the CCC is the use of resistive CuNi wire and brass internal shields. First measurements of 100 pA to 300 pA currents using this CCC are performed at an uncertainty level of around 20 ppm to 50 ppm.

articleTitle: A direct comparison of Josephson Array Voltage Standards
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A number of direct comparisons of Josephson Array Voltage Standards (JAVS) using Superconductor-Insulator-Superconductor (SIS) junction arrays have been performed at the National Metrology Centre (NMC), Singapore. The comparisons were performed over a range of voltage from 1 V to 10 V and with different combinations of array chips, both USA and German made. The comparisons used a parallel biasing method that made it relatively easy to quickly bias both arrays on a nearly matched quantum step. The Type-A uncertainty of the difference voltage was typically lower than 1.5 nV.

articleTitle: Frequency comparison of two fiber-based frequency combs at 633 nm
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Two fiber-based frequency combs were compared at 633 nm. An offset laser was locked to a frequency comb, and the locked laser was measured with another comb. Consequently, the frequency uncertainty of the combs was less than 3 x 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−16</sup> at 10 000 s averaging, which is sufficiently lower than the uncertainty of UTC.

articleTitle: Absolute frequency measurement of an iodine-stabilized 543-nm He-Ne laser with modulation-synchronized phase-locked loop for improved frequency counting
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: An iodine-stabilized 543-nm He-Ne laser is an important laser radiation for the realization of the definition of the meter. These secondary standards should be absolutely measured for traceability to the SI-second. Due to the low power of 543-nm He-Ne lasers, a method to improve the signal-to-noise ratio of this measurement is needed. We use a modulation-synchronized phase-locked loop to lock a slave laser without transferring modulation, thus improving the signal-to-noise ratio through reduced bandwidth and higher optical power. The absolute frequency value thus obtained is in good agreement with the CIPM value.

articleTitle: Ultra-stable frequency dissemination via optical fiber at NICT
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: We have developed an RF dissemination system using optical fiber. The induced phase noise during the transmission is actively cancelled by the compensation system with a VCXO and a loop filter. First proving test was done in the urban telecom fiber link of length 10 km.

articleTitle: Calibration of Rogowski coils at power frequencies using digital sampling
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A high-accuracy system for calibration of Rogowski coils using current transformers and digital sampling is described in the paper. An automated version of the calibration system is capable of operating at currents up to 2,000 A, at power frequencies. A semi-automated version is capable of operating at currents up to 60,000 A. The uncertainty of the calibration system is estimated to be better than 100ldr10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-6</sup>.

articleTitle: Design and fabrication of high value standard resistors at INTI
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: We have designed and fabricated a set of twelve high value standard resistors of 10 MOmega, 100 MOmega and 1 GOmega nominal values. A subset of three of them were measured at NIST during January, 2008, showing to have good stability and design, a short settling time and an important voltage coefficient.

articleTitle: Calibration of the thd functions of electrical standards
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: The paper describes a test procedure, the test waveforms, and the reference equipment used to calibrate the voltage and current total harmonic distortion (THD) measuring functions of multi-function electrical standards. It also shows that it is possible to establish traceability to the SI units for the THD measurements by measuring the voltage and power of the test waveforms with voltmeters and wattmeters that are traceable to SI. Results of recent calibrations are discussed.

articleTitle: Recent progress of an atomic fountain frequency standard NMIJ-F1 (2006 – 2007)
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: We review the current status of development of NMIJ-F1 for the recent two years. We have performed frequency measurement a few times per year with a combined (Type A, Type B) uncertainty of 3.9times10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-15</sup>. For more frequent contribution to keep International Atomic Time (TAI), optics and microwave system have been modified.

articleTitle: Characterization of loading effects in precision 1 Ω resistors
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Precision standard resistors manufactured within the last two decades using improved construction techniques and materials, such as the resistance alloy Evanohm, have been shown to have excellent environmental characteristics. Power dissipation (or loading) effects in several types of resistors have been examined including specifically those made of Manganin and Evanohm, and with the resistor element both sealed within a double wall container, or unsealed. Our recent tests on these resistors demonstrate that conditions of power dissipation within the resistors and the duty cycle of the power applied to the resistor have significant effect on the uncertainty of the measurement.

articleTitle: On the accuracy of two-way satellite time and frequency transfer: A study of triplet closures
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Two-way satellite time and frequency transfer has become an important technical component in the process of the realization of International Atomic Time and also for comparisons among the best primary frequency standards. This paper contains results of studies aimed at improving the knowledge of the uncertainty for true time transfer between remote sites. Our study addresses mostly the collection of so-called time transfer triplets between sites 1, 2, and 3. Systematic deviations from zero in the combination (1-2) + (2-3) + (3-1) would point to incomplete understanding and handling of systematic offsets in the individual time transfers. We show that such offsets exist, but that they are only in specific cases significant (up to about 2 ns), and we discuss possible causes.

articleTitle: ACJVS operating margins using a ternary arbitrary bitstream generator
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: We describe measurements with a pulse-driven AC Josephson voltage standard (ACJVS) that uses a ternary arbitrary bitstream generator as the bias source. From these measurements we conclude that the circuit is operational for voltages up to 220 mV rms. We present a measured spectrum and operating margins for different voltages.

articleTitle: Development of simulant high-power resistor
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Two simulant high-power resistance standards were newly developed at NIM. The first resistance standard uses a high-power resistor for signal sampling, IVD for adjustment, and a voltage-follower for output. The high-power low-resistance resistor has similar input/output characteristic as the simulated variable and can carry more load power. The second resistance standard uses resistance network for current sampling and A/D converter for feeding back the output voltage. They provide a standard for traceability of Earth-Continuity Testers with uncertainty 0.05% to 0.17%, k=2.

articleTitle: Traceability of capacitance measurements at NMI VSL
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: NMi VSL is working on its independent realization of the unit of capacitance (F). The traceability will be derived from the DC quantum hall resistance standard. This paper focuses on a quadrature bridge that has recently been completed. The first results obtained from the bridge show an agreement with the NMi VSL reference group of capacitors within 1 muF/F.

articleTitle: The equivalent circuit of the ac resistor and the equi-potential shielding with 1/2 voltage
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: The ordinary equivalent circuit of the AC resistor is not exact enough when the parasitic parameters of the resistor are considered. At the same time, the traditional shielding with potential equal to the lower voltage terminal of the resistor will contribute additional parasitic capacitance to the resistor and will deteriorate the calculated result of AC/DC difference. Using an equi-potential shielding with 1/2 voltage of the resistor is helpful to decrease the AC/DC resistance difference.

articleTitle: Development of a square-wave based AC Josephson system for AC Voltage metrology
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A square-wave based AC Josephson apparatus is under development at MIKES. A new high-resolution custom made sine wave source has been developed and is being tested. A simple scheme for calibration of thermal converters (TC) with an AC Josephson system is suggested.

articleTitle: Toward a determination of RK at LNE with a new Thompson-Lampard calculable capacitor
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: This paper presents the French project aiming to determine the von Klitzing constant R<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">K</sub> with an uncertainty of one part in 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">8</sup>. The design adopted for a new Thompson-Lampard calculable capacitor and some parts of the impedance comparison measurement chain are presented.

articleTitle: Josephson junction array driven by modulated optical combs
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: We have performed an experiment to drive an over-damped Josephson junction array (JJA) with modulated current pulse trains, which are generated by a modulated optical comb (an ultra-short pulse laser). The intensities of optical pulse trains are modulated using a pulse pattern generator. We quantitatively verified that the output voltages of the JJA were consistent with the modulation signals.

articleTitle: Some applications of times series analysis techniques to coaxial AC bridges
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Results of applying time series analysis techniques to measurements on a coaxial AC bridge are presented. A simple formula is used to account for correlations introduced by a low pass filter, and the Allan variance is applied to a study of sources of noise and instability.

articleTitle: Phase error measurement of resistive current shunt using pulse counting
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: This paper introduces a new method for phase angle measurement of a resistive current shunt using pulse counting technique. The described simple and accurate method provides an advantage that can be realized easily. The system consists of a precision current shunt, wideband buffers, two zero-crossing detector, a phase detector, digital counting circuits, and a pulse counter. Measurement principle compares each other signal that is occurred in the measuring signal and reference signal and measures difference of the signal by pulse counting. An experiment used shunts of 1 A and frequency supplied from 60 Hz to 5 kHz. The difference of phase error was less than 10 murad at 60 Hz. This principle is usable in the frequency range up to 100 kHz.

articleTitle: A quantum current standard based on phase slip
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: We show that it is possible to fabricate a device, based on a superconducting nanowire, to demonstrate the existence of coherent quantum phase slip (QPS). If coherent QPS exists, this device will form the basis of a new type of quantum current standard capable of closing the metrological triangle.

articleTitle: Recent progress in the setup of the electron counting capacitance standard at PTB
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: We report on our new results in the setup of an experiment where a capacitor is charged by a well-known number of electrons. Considerable progress was made by using a single-electron R-pump for the controlled manipulation of single electrons for the first time, and by the successful implementation of a suitable cryogenic capacitor in the millikelvin dilution refrigerator setup.

articleTitle: Correcting for nonideal probe locations in near-field scanning measurements of antenna parameters
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: We discuss efficient near-field to far-field transformation algorithms that relax the usual restriction that data points be located on regular grids on special surfaces (planar, spherical, or cylindrical).

articleTitle: Influence of the optical quality of the interferometer optics on the diameter measurement of the Avogadro silicon sphere
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Within the International Avogadro Project measurements of molar mass and lattice parameter of a silicon single crystal and mass and volume of a high precision silicon sphere made of the same crystal are combined to calculate Avogadro's constant. As an overall uncertainty of 2ldr10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-8</sup> is aimed at, the determination of the volume of the Avogadro sphere requires unequalled precision in absolute interferometry. Especially systematical influences on an experimental setup can only be detected, if relevant influencing parameters can be varied. The spheres interferometer of PTB offers a unique way to investigate the influence of its optical components.

articleTitle: Feasibility study on remote calibration of impedance standard for industrial use
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A feasibility study of remote calibration of impedance standards with a view to industrial use was conducted. Verification tests showed that the values obtained by remote calibration agreed with those by hand-carry calibration within the standard uncertainties.

articleTitle: Active damping control of a torsion pendulum by radiation pressure
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: In this paper, we describe the experiment of using radiation pressure to actively damp a strip torsion pendulum. The radiation source is a 1.5 W Nd:YAG laser with an actively controlled variable attenuator. By controlling the power of the laser, force of nano-newton scale can be generated and used to damp the resonant oscillation of the pendulum. We also quantitatively measured the force due to the radiation pressure. The result is in good agreement with the theoretical prediction.

articleTitle: Low noise silicon CMOS single-electron transistors and electron pumps
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: We design and fabricate single-electron transistors and electron pumps within an industrial CMOS platform. Based on silicon nanowire transistors, these devices allow very simple and stable single-electron control thanks to doping modulation along the wire.

articleTitle: An un-intrusive optically modulated scatterer technique for unwired small antenna measurement
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: In this paper we present an un-intrusive OMS (optically modulated scatterer) technique to measure the radiation pattern of an un-wired small antenna such as an RFID tag. The radiation performance of an RFID antenna is measured without any metallic feeding wire that could disturb the field pattern. The degradation of the field pattern caused by a slab attached to the RFID antenna is also evaluated with this technique.

articleTitle: Uncertainty propagation through network parameter conversions
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: This paper describes a simplified procedure to obtain the uncertainties when transforming VNA measurement results to other sets of network parameters.

articleTitle: The capability of the national institute of standards in the electromagnetic compatibility measurements
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: The serious and increasing form of the environmental pollution due to the electromagnetic interference is a big problem in all countries. Various forms of EMI may cause electrical and electronic malfunctions, can prevent the proper use of the of the radio frequency spectrum, can ignite flammable or other hazardous atmospheres, and may even have a direct effect on human tissue. The threat of EMI is controlled by adopting the practices of electromagnetic compatibility (EMC), currently NIS-Egypt has the facilities to describe the ability of electrical and electronic devices, unit of equipment or systems to operate without interfering with other systems, also describes the ability of such systems to operate as intended within a specified electromagnetic environment according to the EMC directives which determine tests, measurements, limits and the essential requirements that products must satisfied before freely marketed . The paper gives an over view about the EMC lab at NIS showing both its functions and activities.

articleTitle: A four-terminal co-axial pair Maxwell-Wein bridge for the measurement of self-inductance
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A four-terminal co-axial pair Maxwell-Wein bridge has been developed at NRC. The bridge is suitable for the determination of self-inductance in terms of resistance and capacitance in the frequency range of 800 Hz to 5 kHz. The bridge is primarily designed to measure the four-terminal definition of the impedance of a self-inductor but may be easily modified to measure one-terminal pair impedance using a suitable adaptor.

articleTitle: Characterization method of electric field strength sensor by using transfer standard in GTEM cell
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: In the present study, we introduce a wideband calibration method of electric field strength sensors by using a gigahertz transverse electromagnetic (GTEM) cell and a reference electric field sensor. A preliminary comparison shows good agreement between the proposed method and other ones. Another measurement result will be presented at the conference.

articleTitle: Establishment of the open area antenna Calibration Site at CENAM
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: The process to establish an open area antenna calibration test site (calts) as a national reference for Mexico is presented. The site is compliant with CISPR-16-1-5 international standard. The validation of the site according to this standard is described in the paper.

articleTitle: Precision measurement of the FQHE resistance at filling factor 1/3
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A precision measurement of the fractional quantized Hall resistance in a high mobility two-dimensional electron system was carried out as a test of the universality of the quantum Hall effect. Our results indicate that the Hall resistance at filling factor nu=1/3 does not deviate from the theoretical value 3ldrh/e<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> within a relative uncertainty of plusmn3.3 parts in 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">8</sup> (k=2).

articleTitle: Development of a compact 1.54 μm acetylene standard at NPL
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A compact and simplified <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">13</sup>C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> optical frequency standard is currently under development at NPL. The standard uses an inexpensive, commercially available 20 mW DFB diode laser, which is stabilized to line P(16) of the nu<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub> + nu<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> band at 1542 nm in an experimental arrangement which dispenses with the need for an enhancement cavity. Preliminary stability and reproducibility data will be presented.

articleTitle: Progress towards the redefinition of the kilogram: Measurements of Planck’s constant using watt balances
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: The watt balance compares electrical power and mechanical power to determine Planck's constant h in SI units. If the definition of the kilogram in the SI is altered to fix the value of Planck's constant this will remove the last artefact standard from the SI and the watt balance will provide a way to realise the SI mass unit. At present there are three operational watt balances, with more planned or under construction. Two laboratories, NIST and NPL, have published results from their experiments. These results differ significantly and further work is required to discover the source of the discrepancy.

articleTitle: Configurable unit for precise RMS measurements
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A system for the precise measurement of electrical quantities by means of the rms value of ac voltages or currents is described. The system is implemented by a multijunction thermal converter and low cost electronic circuits. As a first application the system can both carry out ac voltage comparisons and ac and dc voltage measurements.

articleTitle: Automated 10 volt Josephson voltage standard system operating with liquid helium and with a cryocooler
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A commercially available complete microprocessor controlled, fully automated 10 Volt Josephson voltage standard system was developed in cooperation between IPHT and Supracon. The system operates with an array of altogether 19,700 SIS Josephson tunnel junctions. A direct comparison between two such systems showed an uncertainty of 2 times 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-10</sup>. Furthermore, a novel cryocooler based system is described.

articleTitle: Operation of a 10-V programmable Josephson voltage standard system with a 10-K compact cryocooler
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: We have been operating a 10-V programmable Josephson voltage standard (PJVS) system that was developed based on a multi-chip technique. We compared the PJVS with an SIS-based conventional JVS indirectly using a zener diode. The results agreed within 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-8</sup> level.

articleTitle: Correction of systematic errors due to the voltage leads in AC Josephson Voltage Standard
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: NIST recently reported the first application of a quantum AC Josephson voltage standard (ACJVS) for calibration of thermal transfer standards in the 1 kHz to 10 kHz frequency range. This paper describes preliminary work on extending its frequency calibration range up to 100 kHz by correcting systematic errors due to voltage leads.

articleTitle: Simple algorithm for sampling synchronization of ADCs
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: This paper describes a simple and easy to implement algorithm for synchronizing analog-to-digital converters to the fundamental of a continuous periodic signal. It is based on the discrete-Fourier transform (DFT) on sampled data and uses DFT-leakage detection to ensure a synchronous sampling. It may be applied to distorted waveforms in general, irrespective of the type of ADC used, and no windowing functions on sampled data need to be applied.

articleTitle: Uncorrelated Gaussian noise assumption in harmonic analysis with integrating digital sampling voltmeters
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Uncorrelated Gaussian noise is often assumed when estimating the harmonic parameters of periodic signals from digitized data. It is demonstrated here that the noise at the output of high-resolution integrating digital sampling voltmeters can be regarded uncorrelated for all practical purposes when white noise is added to the input signal.

articleTitle: Direct broadband microwave characterization of biological tissues using the coaxial probe technique
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A key advantage of using coaxial probe for microwave characterization of biological media is the non-invasive nature of the technique. The complex permittivities of normal tissues from animals and both normal and cancerous tissues from human bodies were measured over a broadband microwave region with this technique. The biological tissue measurements showed that the complex permittivities measured by this technique are in good agreement with other investigations. This is a cost effective, non invasive and easy to use technique which makes it very suitable for diagnostic and therapeutic applications of microwaves in biomedicine.

articleTitle: Techniques for the calibration of interharmonic generators in support of low frequency immunity compliance testing (IEC61000-4-13)
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A description of the interference immunity testing of electrical products is given and the need for traceable calibration of the associated testing generators is described. A brief presentation of three analysis algorithms to calibrate testing generators is given.

articleTitle: A new approach for steering UTC(KRIS)
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: This paper describes development of a steering strategy that is intended for improving the stability of UTC(KRIS). The resultant time scale is realized by steering an active H-maser via carrier-phase (CP) GPS time transfer. Emphasis is placed on the fact that a real-time GPS CP time transfer is utilized to compute the time difference between the time scale and GPS time. The Kalman estimator is utilized to form a Linear Quadratic Gaussian (LQG) controller. The relative performance assessment is conducted in terms of the frequency predictability and time instability by comparing against the current time scale of UTC(KRIS).

articleTitle: A multistage technique for current transformers with current ratios of less than unity
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: An overview of the development and performance of a current transformer with current ratios of less than unity at the National Research Council of Canada (NRC) is described. A prototype current transformer with a current ratio of 0.025A/1A that can be operated at up to at least ten times the rated current (secondary current up to ges 10 A), with ratio errors of less than 20times10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-6</sup> in both magnitude and phase with burdens up to 0.1 Omega and at frequencies up to 1000 Hz has been developed.

articleTitle: Comparision scattering coefficient measurements by broad-band methods from 2 — 18 GHz using type N connectors
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: This paper presents the results of GT-RF international key comparison CCEM.RF-K5b.CL for the measurement of scattering coefficients over the range of 2-18 GHz. Nineteen National Metrology Institutes were involved in this comparison, which took place between June 2003 and November 2006. On the whole, the results show a good agreement amongst the participants.

articleTitle: Probing mobility gaps at resistivity minima in the integer quantum hall effect
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Magneto-transport measurements are performed on the AlGaAs/GaAs quantum Hall (QH) devices fabricated recently by our group. A series of Hall plateaus are observed with increasing the perpendicular magnetic field, and the mobility gaps resulting from localization effects are investigated at the minima in the longitudinal resistivity. Only the gap corresponding to the filling factor i = 2 is close to the expected cyclotron energy, and our study supports that the low-field QH conductors may suffer problems due to insufficient localization. The anomalous change on the Hall slope is observed when the i = 3 plateau is destroyed by the large current.

articleTitle: The properties of commercial thick film resistance elements as ac-dc transfer standards
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A new set of ac-dc resistance transfer standards are being developed for use in the BIPM quadrature bridge. These resistors use commercial thick film resistance elements, whose small ac-dc difference is calibrated against a calculable coaxial reference. The improved stability of the new resistors should reduce the overall uncertainty of the quadrature transfer.

articleTitle: Air-gap characterization of the LNE watt balance magnetic circuit
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: The magnetic circuit built for the LNE watt balance experiment is now assembled and its characterization is in progress. We describe here the methods used and give the first results.

articleTitle: Determination of the correction factor of a waveguide microcalorimeter
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A novel, self-consistent approach for the determination of the correction factor of a waveguide microcalorimeter is described. The method is based on the measurement of offset shorts of different length followed by one single calibration measurement of an unknown thermistor DUT. Without precisely measuring the RF power incident to the reference plane, both calibration factor of the DUT as well as the calorimeter correction factor are determined. The method theoretically takes into account the different surface current distributions and associated waveguide losses being existent for the offset short as well as for the DUT measurements. It has been applied to a recently developed PTB twin-type microcalorimeter (33-50 GHz) resulting in low uncertainties of the effective efficiency of thermistor power sensors.

articleTitle: Accuracy comparison among different mathematical models of coaxial microcalorimeter
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: INRiM coaxial microcalorimeter underwent to several modifications concerning both hardware and software in the last decade. Several models have been meanwhile proposed, each one considering different calibration processes and error sources. Hereby we compare these models for the 3.5 mm configuration from 10 MHz to 26.5 GHz.

articleTitle: Laboratory experiment of 9.2 GHz frequency transfer through a fiber
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: We report the preliminary laboratory experiment on transferring of a 9.2 GHz frequency through a 10 km commercial 1550 nm fiber in NIM. Using beat signal of the two side bands of 4.6 GHz phase modulation as transferring frequency, the sensitivity of actively compensating is significantly enhanced. We have obtained a stability of about 3E-15/1000s up to now only with slow loop servo.

articleTitle: Development of a light source with a sub-hertz linewidth for an Yb optical lattice clock
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A light source to drive the <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>-<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>P<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sub> transition in Yb atoms is generated by two solid state lasers: a Nd:YAG laser and a Yb:YAG laser, using a sum-frequency generation (SFG) scheme. SFG power of about 22 mW is obtained at the required frequency.

articleTitle: A new LCR meter right angle phase self-calibration method for use in rf resistance calibrations by using capacitance standards
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: This paper describes how to calibrate the right angle phase of a Four-Terminal-Pair (4TP) LCR meter. The meter uses the right angle signal to process synchronous detector as a vector receiver. The right angle calibration method uses, at least, one programmable phase signal generator and a phase shift circuits. The signal generator and the phase shifter do not require a precision 90 degree angle. As a result, the right angle phase deviation of the LCR meter is better than 100 murad at 10 MHz. This method is also applicable to the phase calibration of a vector network analyzer.

articleTitle: An experimental evaluation of a cryogenic noise source by a sliding short method in the frequency range of 8 GHz to 12 GHz
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A cryogenic noise source (CNS) cooled by liquid nitrogen (LN<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>) is constructed and evaluated in the frequency range of 8 GHz to 12 GHz (WR-90 waveguide band). A noise temperature of the CNS is changed from the boiling temperature of LN<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> by a correction factor (CF) related to loss and temperature distribution of a transmission line (TL). We have investigated the CF by a sliding short method using a total-power radiometer. Comparison results of the noise temperature by the radiometer with two calibrated noise sources proved validity of the CF.

articleTitle: Reducing the uncertainty in a measure of the acceleration of gravity for the electronic kilogram
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Calculating the force on a reference mass for the electronic kilogram experiment requires using both absolute and relative gravity meters to measure the acceleration of gravity. Tests have been conducted to achieve an uncertainty of less than 1 part in 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">8</sup>.

articleTitle: A Kelvin resistance bridge with the frequency range from dc to 100 kHz
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: For the accurate measurement and calibration of the famous Tinsley 5685 AC standard resistors, a new type of Kelvin resistance bridge working over frequency range from DC to 100 kHz is described. At the same time, a bridge substitution technique is used in which the unknown Tinsley resistor is compared to the standard of AC/DC calculable resistor with double helix arrangement. Through this bridge the frequency characteristics of these portable AC standard resistors with the resistance value from 1 Omega to 10 kOmega have been obtained, which will extend their frequency range in metrology calibration.

articleTitle: Sampling error analysis applied to high-accuracy measurements
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: In this paper we apply a mathematical analysis of the main error sources in sampling theory to estimate alias and integration errors in asynchronous digital sampling measurements.

articleTitle: A new approach to determine phase shift of shunt based on the sampling measurement and substitution method
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A new approach to determine phase-shift of shunt based on the sampling measurement and substitution method is described with theoretical analysis and test results. The differences with SP’s results are within 2 μrad at fundamental wave of 50 Hz and within 30 μrad at 30<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> harmonic.

articleTitle: Thermally controlled gas-dielectric standard capacitors constructed at inmetro
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Gas-dielectric standard capacitors have a temperature coefficient of (0 plusmn 2) muF/F per K. This is too high for deriving the capacitance unit from the quantum Hall resistance. A standard capacitor was thermally controlled to reduce by two orders of magnitude its temperature variation. The construction details and the experimental results are discussed.

articleTitle: Balance pan damping using tuned sloshing liquids
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: This paper describes a new method to damp out balance pan oscillations even when the balance is operated in vacuum. The key is to tune the wavelength of the damping liquid, which resides in a sealed container attached above the pan, to the natural frequencies expected in the pan operation. Both NIST and LNE are investigating the practical application of this damping approach in our respective watt balance experiments.

articleTitle: Free space antenna facor evaluation of logperiodic antenna using time-domain and pulse compression techniques
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: We have proposed the method for evaluating the free-space antenna factor of a log-periodic broadband antenna (LPDA) with time-domain technique [1] [2]. Our method is based on the techniques of time domain analysis and pulse compression techniques. The proposed method enables us to isolate the direct wave from the reflected waves on the ground plane in an open area test site, and to evaluate the free-space antenna factor. In this paper, we explain the free-space antenna factors and its uncertainty of our proposed method.

articleTitle: A new short-bar method for 4TP admittance standards calibration by using modified Z-matrix expression to improve S/N for higher impedance
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: This paper describes how to calibrate four-terminal-pair (4TP) admittance standards using a new short-bar method with modified Z-matrix expression containing a correction term. The short-bar method is to measure the signal to correspond to the standard with better S/N for higher impedance standard, especially 1 pF. Therefore a 1 pF capacitor can be calibrated containing the direct measurement at reporting frequencies. As this method does not require the equivalent circuit, it can be applied to general 4TP admittance calibration.

articleTitle: Realization of the Henry at METAS
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: This paper describes a measurement set up based on a synchronous sampling system which allows the realization of the henry directly from the ohm and the second. This new set up improved the realization of the henry at METAS by a factor of 5. For the calibration of a 100 mH inductance standard at a frequency of 1 kHz, the expanded uncertainty amounts now to 15 muH/H.

articleTitle: RF-dc difference measurement system at NMC
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: This paper describes an automated RF-dc transfer difference measurement system developed at the National Metrology Centre, Singapore. The system uses calculable single junction thermal voltage converters as primary standards and various high frequency reference thermal converter standards to measure the RF-dc voltage transfer difference for frequency range from 100 kHz to 100 MHz at voltage range from 0.5 V to 10 V.

articleTitle: A new self-calibration method for a decade inductive voltage divider by using bifilar windings as an essential standard at wide frequency
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: This paper describes how to calibrate a Self-Calibration Decade Inductive Voltage Divider (S-IVD). The S-IVD consists of windings of a decade main-divider and nine bifilar windings as an essential standard. A commercial Four-Terminal-Pair (4TP) LCR meter is used for measuring the differential vector voltage of the S-IVD. It does not require injection signals for balancing. The S-IVD can be calibrated obtaining a few parts in 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">8</sup> to in 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sup> uncertainty at 120 Hz to 1 MHz. Another IVD as a Device Under Test (DUT) can be calibrated by 1:1 direct comparison using the S-IVD.

articleTitle: Development of microcontroller-based signal synthesizers for AC reference standards
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: This paper presents the realization of a compact two- channel microcontroller-based digital synthesizer (CMDS) for generating accurate alternating (ac) voltage signals aiming at improving ac measurement techniques at AIST. Device description and the measurement techniques employed for evaluating it are described. First evaluations indicate that the CMDS may be used in high-grade ac Metrology.

articleTitle: Modified Maxwell-Wien bridge with auto source balance
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: This paper describes the realization of auto source balance in a modified Maxwell-Wien bridge by using a differential amplifier. The method of eliminating the oscillation of this differential amplifier is also discussed. The inductance measurement error introduced by the adoption of differential amplifier and related compensation circuit has also been analyzed in details. In the range of 100 μH∼100 H, the inductance measurement error caused by the amplifier is less than 2 ppm under 1 kHz .

articleTitle: Analysis of results in complex-valued intercomparisons
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: In this paper a Figure of Merit (FoM) for evaluation of agreement between participants in complex-valued intercomparisons is proposed. Our purpose is to judge the quality of the results and of the uncertainty regions as provided by the participants. Any change in the measured values or in the size, shape and orientation of the uncertainty ellipses is shown to correspond itself with a variation in the FoM of a given participant.

articleTitle: SIM comparison of dc resistance at 1 Ω, 1 MΩ, and 1 GΩ
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A regional comparison of DC resistance standards at the nominal values of 1 Omega, 1 MOmega, and 1 GOmega has recently been completed in the Sistema Interamericano de Metrogia (SIM) region. The motivation, design, standards, and results of this regional comparison are reported.

articleTitle: An audio frequency multiplier with planar thermal converters for power measurements
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A multiplier based on thermal converters was developed for the use in broad band power measurements. The topology of the multiplier is of simple design and suppresses its static errors by means of an improved summing circuit. It employs fast synchronous ac-dc transfer technique to shorten the measurement time. The evaluated measurement uncertainties are of the order of some 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-6</sup> for frequencies up to 20 kHz and some 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-5</sup> for frequencies up to 100 kHz.

articleTitle: Development of AC current comparator based on coaxial cable for enlarging measurement frequency range up to 10 kHz
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: We have started a study in 2005 for enlarging the frequency range of the AC current measurement using a current comparator up to 10 kHz. In this study, it is the most important to make the error factor of the comparator clear and the intensity of them estimate. Therefore, we designed the new comparator aimed for the evaluation of the error experimentally. For improving reliability of self-calibration result at the comparator, a decimal system was adopted to winding construction. By observing the potential distribution at the coaxial cable at current comparison windings, it made dominant error current clearly. The nominal primary current of the comparator is 100 A, and range 1/1-1/500, of the ratio, the limit of the frequency is 10 kHz. By the ratio within 100, we assume the uncertainty of the comparator as the current ratio standard after correction to be the order of 50 muA/A.

articleTitle: Compact extended port capable of full 2-port calibrations using optical techniques
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: We have developed a compact extended port using optical techniques that can be used with full 2-port calibrations such as SOLT, SOLR, TRL, and et al. This extended port is an advanced and compact version of the extended port developed previously [1]. All components of the compact extended port are included in an aluminum box whose size is 2 cm x 2 cm x 5.6 cm. An N-type male connector is attached to the box. Because only optical fibers are connected to the box, there is no metal except the box and the connector.

articleTitle: Development and application of a programmable PD calibrator
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A programmable partial discharge calibrator is described, which is constituted by an arbitrary waveform generator series connected to a capacitor. The step voltage waveform supplied by the generator is software controlled. The characteristics and the capabilities of the calibrator are presented and the procedures adopted for its characterization are reported. Using the calibrator, the performances of four partial discharge measuring systems, equipped with analog and digital measuring instruments, are investigated and compared.

articleTitle: SNS josephson junction series arrays for the Josephson Arbitrary Waveform Synthesizer
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: AC voltages and arbitrary waveforms are synthesized by Josephson junctions operated by short current pulses. Series arrays of intrinsically shunted SNS Josephson junctions were developed and investigated for applications in this Josephson Arbitrary Waveform Synthesizer (JAWS). Amplitudes above 200 mV were generated by series arrays consisting of more than 10,000 junctions arranged in a meander-like design.

articleTitle: Generation of reference low frequency electric fields by TEM cells
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: This paper deals with the use of TEM cells for the calibration of low frequency electric field meters. The non uniformity of the spatial field distribution and the perturbation caused by the probe support type and positioning are investigated with the aim of evaluating their influence on the field actually experienced by the probe. The analysis is developed through a boundary element model, and validated by experimental evidences.

articleTitle: Improved high input impedance mV-amplifiers with gain factors from 10 to 900
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: New mV-amplifiers driving a planar multijunction thermal converter (PMJTC) at their output have been developed to measure the output voltage of micropotentiometers (mupots). Using a twin-stage design with gains of 10, 20 and 30 per stage, total gain factors from 10 to 900 are achieved. This results in a usable range of input voltages from 100 muV up to 100 mV at frequencies from dc to 1 MHz. A novel offset compensation allows reliable operation also at higher gain factors. The ac-dc transfer difference if flat to within plusmn 300 muV/V up to 1 MHz.

articleTitle: Evaluation of low-frequency characteristic of a thermal converter using a programmable josephson voltage standard
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A new dual-heater thermal voltage converter (DH- TVC) with improved low-frequency performance has been developed at the AIST. Frequency characteristic of the DH-TVC was evaluated using a dual-output programmable Josephson voltage standard(DO-PJVS), and was confirmed to have low-frequency flatness better than 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-6</sup> down to 1 Hz.

articleTitle: Uncertainty budget for the NIM QHR standard system
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: In this paper, the uncertainty of the QHR standard system at NIM is estimated and the combined standard uncertainty is given out. A new method to calibrate CCC ratio unit working in-situ is introduced.
