articleTitle: A proposal of definition for uncertainty of harmonic voltage and its experimental dermination
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A definition for uncertainty of harmonic voltage is proposed. A conception of “characteristic signal” is discussed for digital estimation of equipment. The experimental determination for the uncertainty sources such as leakage, noise and non-linearity from frequencies are reported. Within the 60<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> harmonic up to the range of 500 V, the uncertainty reference to fundamental is less than 30 μV/V (k=2).

articleTitle: Precision frequency measurement of the 2S1/2 — 2F7/2 electric octupole transition in a single 171Yb+ ion
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: We report precision laser spectroscopy of the <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1/2</sub> (F = 0, m<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">F</sub>=0)-<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>F<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7/2</sub> (F =3, m<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">F</sub>= 0) clock transition in a single, trapped, laser cooled ion of <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">171</sup>Yb<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup>. The absolute frequency is measured to be 642 121 496 772 656 (12) Hz, a factor of 20 more accurate than previous measurements.

articleTitle: A new error compensation method of inductive voltage divider
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: This paper describes a new error compensation method based on the transformer principle. The method makes use of the voltage transformer being connected in parallel to input of IVD to provide n voltage value of n times 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-8</sup>, which can respectively compensate in-phase error and quadrature error of each output tap voltage of IVD by regulating n. After compensation, the accuracy of IVD can stably achieve n times 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-8</sup>.

articleTitle: Hall resistance plateaus in high quality graphene samples at large currents: Toward quantization tests
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Graphene Hall bars prepared from exfoliated natural graphite of large size and high quality have been measured in the quantum Hall effect regime. The monolayer Graphene sheet shows Hall quantization robust upon applying very large current. Low longitudinal resistance is found up to 10 muA with finite width h/2e<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> Hall plateau at 4.2 K and 16 T. The TiAu/Graphene contact resistance is found low, typically 20 Omega to 50 Omega. The results strongly indicate that Graphene is a promising new material for quantum metrology.

articleTitle: Design and construction of Zeeman slower for 87Sr optical clock at NIM
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: In this paper, a Zeeman slower suitable for Sr optical clock was designed and constructed through optimizing the winding number. The root mean squared deviations of the experimental data from theoretical data and computed data from theoretical data are both less than 0.5%.

articleTitle: Research on digital optical fiber current transformer with CT power supply
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A digital optical fiber current transformer (OCT) based on Rogowski coil and optical fiber transmission for use in high voltage systems is described in this paper. The technologies of signal sampling, processing and communication for the optical current transformer are introduced. The paper analyzes the present supply power techniques on high voltage side, and puts forward a new closed-loop regulating method through tailor-made small CT to obtain stable supply power. The experiment results verified that the designed power supply can operate normally as the current of bus is above 8A. The accuracy of current measurement is 0.2%.

articleTitle: A two-way Josephson voltage standard comparison between NIST and NRC
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A two-way Josephson voltage standard (JVS) direct comparison between the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) and the National Research Council (NRC) has been conducted. The process consists of two comparisons, one using NIST designed hardware and software and the other using NRC designed hardware and software. The results of the two comparisons are in agreement to within 0.7 nV and their mean indicates that the difference between the two JVSs at 10 V is -0.28 nV with a pooled combined uncertainty of 2.07 nV (k=2).

articleTitle: Precision transmittance measurements on ferrites in millimeter waves
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: This paper presents transmittance spectra and complex magnetic permeability and dielectric permittivity parameters of pure and mixed powdered barium ferrites, nickel zinc manganese ferrites and nickel cobalt copper ferrites in a broad-band millimeter wave frequency range. A free space, millimeter wave magneto-optical approach has been successfully employed for precise characterization of ferrite materials. Frequency dependences of the magnetic permeability of ferrites have been calculated using Schlomann's equation for partially magnetized ferrites.

articleTitle: Low-cost high-performance current shunts — improved design for 30 mA – 100 mA
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A new and improved design of the JV current shunts for 30 to 100 mA has been developed. The new shunts use surface-mount resistors mounted in a star configuration. AC-DC difference less than 3 muA/A at 100 kHz and less than 5 muA/A at 300 kHz has been achieved. Calculated and measured values agree very well.

articleTitle: The calibration of IEC standard flickermeters using complex modulated signals
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Flickermeter calibrations currently rely on the predicted response of a standard flickermeter to basic waveforms. A description is given of an interpretation and implementation of the IEC standard flickermeter, developed at NPL, in order to assess the response of commercial flickermeters to more complex waveforms, which are representative of signals that occur in practice. A description of the incorporation of the resulting model into a calibration system for flickermeters under complex-waveform conditions is given.

articleTitle: Calibration of the step response of a 70 GHz sampling oscilloscope using a novel optoelectronic technique
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: We introduce a novel optoelectronic technique for the characterization of the full step response of ultrafast sampling oscilloscopes. The uncertainty of the step response measurement is derived from a Monte-Carlo analysis. The enhanced experimental and theoretical method allows us to specify the rise-time of the step response with a considerably reduced uncertainty as compared to our previous calibration technique.

articleTitle: Constant-voltage steps at 0.1 Volt from a series array of high-Tc Josephson junctions
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: By employing an array of 620 high-T<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub> Josephson junctions, we have achieved a maximum quantum output voltage with approximate value of 0.1 V at a temperature of 79.2 K and a frequency of 77.465 GHz. We also demonstrate that steps on the current-voltage characteristic of an array of bicrystal junctions at voltages of 70 mV were flat over the current range of 150 muA with a relative uncertainty of 0.04 ppm.

articleTitle: Comparison of the technical performance for different designs of single junction thermal converters
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: The technical characteristics of four different designs of single junction thermal converters (SJTCs) are evaluated in this paper. This variety in the designs represents the technical trials in developing enhanced thermoelements and in minimizing the values of their transfer errors. A traceable automated system was used to investigate the time responses, DC reversal difference, and the voltage and frequency dependences. The comparison was performed at the rated current, 5 mA, for frequencies from 10 Hz to 100 kHz. In addition, simulations of the electrical characteristics of the four samples were performed, extending the investigation of the frequency dependence up to 1 MHz. A brief description of the uncertainty statement is also included.

articleTitle: An improved automated calibration system for 10V DC reference
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: This paper describes an DC voltage calibration system which is improved to be more accurate and more easy to operate. It is based on 10 V Josephson array, and uses a fully automated system consisting of switches setup well designed for accurate measurement. An overall standard uncertainty is estimated less than 5 nV(1sigma) at 10 V level.

articleTitle: Coaxial shunts for the ac-dc transfer standards of current
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A new type of coaxial shunts, with nominal current from 20 mA to 20 A have been designed at I.N.RI.M.. Different approaches have been used to built them, depending on their nominal current. In the currents between 100 mA and 20 A they are made as a disk structure, using either SMD resistors or manganin foils. In order to reduce stray effects, their structures have ideally no common magnetic interaction between the input current and the output voltage, allowing a flat response in a wide frequency range.

articleTitle: Fiber-based acetylene-stabilized laser
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: We describe a fiber-based acetylene-stabilized laser, where light is coupled to free-space only to pass through the acetylene cell. The system is constructed using standard components, which makes the approach cost effective and straightforward to implement. The Doppler-free spectrum of acetylene is detected using a simple collinear pump-probe geometry, even without a lock-in amplifier, when the length of the optical path in the spectroscopy arrangement is dithered to cancel interference inevitably present in a fiber-based setup. The third-harmonic technique is used to lock the laser to an acetylene line. The method to cancel the interference can be conceivably used also in laser-stabilization in general.

articleTitle: Capacitance calibration based on two ac quantum hall resistances
publicationTitle: 2008 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: We report on the precise calibration of capacitance standards based on two independent ac quantum Hall resistances. The capacitance is thereby traced to a quantum standard of impedance. The advantages of the realized chain and experimental tests of the coaxial ac bridges involved will be discussed.
